## Top 10 WordPress Tweaks

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/top-10-wordpress-tweaks/

### Top 10 WordPress Tweaks

#### Speed Optimisation

# Top 10 WordPress Tweaks

The WordPress CMS (Content Management System) can be a lot to get your head around, especially for beginners. Prosperity Media have decided to make a list of the top 10 tweaks you may or may not know exist, or have not used in a while to brush up your webmaster skills.

**How to Change the Number of Posts on a Page & Feed**

To control how your blog is displayed to others, you can make changes to the reading settings which adjusts how your blog is viewed by others. You can access it via your Settings then Reading page on the WP Admin dashboard.

The default setting is 10 but it can be changed. Having more can potentially impact load times & therefore having less should decrease page load times.

Here is an example of the post change option:

The syndication feed lets you display how many latest posts you want to be displayed in the RSS feed which you can then submit to aggregators, the URL of the feed is e.g. “example.com/feed/”.

You can also select how long you want to posts to be in the feed, you can either show the full text or you can display 55 words to concise the post & allow users to read the full article to get more information.

**How To Change the WordPress Homepage**

WordPress allows the webmaster to choose whether they want to display the latest posts from their website to display on the homepage or a separate page made specifically for the homepage. Here is how to switch between the two options:

1. Log into the admin section of WordPress via wp-admin.
2. Click the “Settings” menu item in the left sidebar to expand the “Settings” submenu & then click on the “Reading” tab.
3. Once you are there then you have arrived on the page to make the changes. To make the front page display a page click on the radio button called “A static page” in the “Front Page Displays” options, from there you can use the drop down to select which page you would like to display on the front page.
4. To display simply select the “Your Latest Posts” radio button and your latest posts will display on the homepage.
5. Save your changes at the bottom of the page & this will finalize changes you have made.

**Change Admin Username in WordPress Backend**

An important aspect of security for a WordPress CMS website is changing the default username. This is because there have been many attempted hackers trying to break into websites when the default username ‘admin’ has been used.

Here are the steps on how to change your username:

1. Hover over “Users” & select “Add New”
2. Add in the “New User” information
3. Select the role selection as “Administrator”
4. Then click the “Add New User” button & you’re done.
5. You can now view your new “admin” user.
6. Now log out of the existing account.
7. Log in to the new account you just created.
8. Now type in your new WordPress admin username and password and click Log In
9. From the left-hand menu click on Users
10. Delete the original admin account.*
11. Now select your new account you create to attribute the old admin posts to it. (if you do not attribute posts they will be deleted).

You have now completed changing the username successfully.

*Always backup your database before making major changes to your website.

**Use an Email instead of a Username on Login**

Using email an can be just as good as using a unique username & sometimes it could even be better for security as emails are a lot harder to guess making the security stronger.

**Screen Options Usage**

The Screen Options menu is a section on the WordPress administration backend which is located on the top right corner of your blog on certain pages, allowing you to make changes to what you can see on the admin page.

What it contains is a list of boxes which can be checked or unchecked which allows admins to show or hide different sections of an admin screen.

These screen options give the admin a lot more control of what they are able to see & therefore can make you backend usage of the CMS a lot more productive seeing only the elemants you want to see on the page.

**Image SEO**

When performing Image SEO, it is all about ensuring your images can be easily crawled & indexed by the search engines such as Google. With [web crawlers & algorithms](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/google-tweaks-algorithm-panda-4-0-australian-analysis-project/) improving every day, especially at detecting elements in images, the right plan moving forward is to ensure the image can be easy to find via search engines. Below we have listed several ways this can be archived:

- Use an image that matches your text description
- Name the image file appropriately
- Use the “alt” tag for the image with relevant text
- Ensure image dimensions match the image
- Use “srcset” tag wherever it’s feasible
- Compress image to smallest file size possible yet still viewable
- Add OpenGraph tag
- Add Twitter Card tag
- Align images to the centre or to the right for enhanced UX
- Insert image URLs in your sitemaps

**Perfect word count on blog posts**

Here is a guide on the word count of general blog posts & the sort of engagement you should expect depending on the length of the post from The Write Practice blog. A caveat is this guide is for established sites with traffic as sites with no traffic will not see any social shares or comments.

- Blog posts 75 to 300 words in length: Short posts at this length are most suited to creating a discussion focal point with the main disadvantage being the lack of social shares & poor on the SEO front.
- Blog posts 300 to 600 words in length: This is the standard length for an article or blog post as it is quite easy to write, requires minimal in-depth research to get your point across & is considered a great middle ground for gaining social shares & comments, with the drawback being it is not ideal for SEO as it may be to thin.
- Blog posts 750 words in length: This article length is ideal for getting shares & links as it is long enough to have substance but not too long to bore the audience, search engines favour this content when other websites do not provide anything more in-depth.
- Blog posts 1000 to 1500 words in length: Expect to get fewer comments as there will be fewer questions asked due to the content covering most basis of the topic at hand.

**Text Widget Fundamentals**

Here are a few great tips on how to use the text/HTML widget box which is a default widget plugin that comes installed with WordPress right out of the box.

- Adding HTML

According to the official [WordPress](https://en.support.wordpress.com/widgets/text-widget/) support guide, the best practice for adding an HTML widget would be to use the custom box & place your desired content within the widget box as there is minimal risk to code breaking the website.

- Adding an Image

You can add an image to a widget using the custom widget (text) & used the “img src” HTML tag to insert any images you desire, you can then easily change the dimensions via HTML outputting your desired image.

- Adding a Video

There are two ways you could do this, one is to insert a video via the custom HTML text widget, but the second & more practical way is to insert the video into a video widget or a [youtube](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/youtube-seo-services/) video widget which you could easily download from the WordPress plugin library.

- Adding an Audio player

Similar to adding a video, you can insert an audio player by insert a HTML code into the text widget or you could download a audio playing widget such as the soundcloud widget from the wordpress plugin page.

**Remove underscores & replace with dashes**

This is used to improve [both the SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) and the user experience of the website. This can be changed by going into the permalinks via the WordPress admin dashboard then to Settings and finally Permalinks.

Selected the option ‘custom structure’ & put this in /%postname%/

Then when you make a post ensure that dashes are used in the URL for the article.

**Take underlines out of page links**

WordPress has taken the advice of its community onboard & implemented some of the suggestions recommended. One of the major changes is the drop-down menu has moved to the top row of buttons while the horizontal rule and strikethrough buttons have moved to the second row.

The underline and justify buttons are no longer available in version 4.7 & above as sometimes the underlining text causes confusion due to the reader misinterpreting the underline for a link.

It is therefore recommended to update your WordPress blog to the latest version if you have not already done so to ensure you are experiencing the best backend WordPress has to offer.

Here are some before & after screenshots of the text editor backend:

Before (with underline button)

After (Without underline button)

It is now also easier to find out what button does what with a shortcut describing what each button does opos up when you hover over it ensuring the best user experience of the CMS.

**Final remarks**

And that is a wrap, I hope you enjoyed the tips & learned something new to add to your WordPress repertoire. These tips should keep your WordPress website secure & ensure you have a few additional productivity hacks to add to your knowledge basket.

Another great tip as an added bonus makes sure to update your WordPress website regularly, ensuring you have backed up the website in the process just in case there are any unforeseen errors or compatibility issues.

Which tip did you like the most? Feel free to like comment or share any feedback or additional tips you may have.

## TikTok SEO Strategies

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/tiktok-seo/

### TikTok SEO: Grow Your TikTok Organically

#### SEO

# TikTok SEO: Grow Your TikTok Organically

TikTok is the new kid on the block when it comes to online marketing.

This means there’s plenty of opportunity but also lots of mystery…

How are you supposed to know what works and what doesn’t?

Plus, millions of TikTok videos are posted every single day so it’s becoming more and more difficult to stand out.

That’s why we decided to write this post, to bring you everything we’ve learned about TikTok SEO.

Especially now that Google can index TikTok videos, we’ve been utilising a ‘*search everywhere*’ approach to our SEO strategies. 

To make use of our experience, [send our team a message](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/contact/) to find out more about our TikTok SEO services. 

## TikTok SEO Strategy

There are several methods that our Tiktok [SEO agency](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) incorporates to boost the profiles of clients’ pages. 

To get the best results you’ll need to implement all of them while frequently posting new content.

Fortunately for you, we’ve picked up a few TikTok SEO tips that we’ll share below.

### Keyword Research

Keyword research on TikTok is different from most other search engines like Google.

You will need to get creative in order to find what users are searching for.

One trick is to use TikTok’s Keyword Insights tool to find trending keywords.

All you have to do is enter the topic you want ideas for and it will return a load of keywords for you.

Depending on your niche you may want to start broad with your search terms and then get more specific so you can see the popularity of your niche.

This tool provides a comprehensive breakdown of keywords, along with their popularity, popularity change, and click-through rate.

By using this tool, you can gain a deeper understanding of TikTok and optimize your content accordingly.

A simpler way to do things is to use the search bar in the TikTok app.

Start by entering relevant keywords in the TikTok search bar and looking at the auto-populated suggestions.

Say your TikTok focuses on makeup tutorials, tips, and reviews.

Type “Makeup” into the search bar with variations of common search terms such as “Makeup for” or “Best makeup”

Take a look at the suggestions that Tiktok auto-fills; there are going to be loads of content ideas.

To go one step further, you can take common search phrases and keep adding letters of the alphabet for even more suggestions.

Repeat this process until you have compiled a list of relevant keywords that align with your content.

Because there are so many keyword ideas, don’t feel pressure to create content on all of them.

Only choose the ones that fit in with the style of TikTok you have or want to create.

**TIP**: From our analysis, we’ve found that keywords on TikTok and [YouTube](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/youtube-seo-services/) are very similar. Seen as there are more research tools available for YouTube, you could leverage them for keyword research on TikTok. 

### Hashtag Research

When you’re doing your keyword research take note of the hashtags popular videos are using.

You can also go to TikTok’s Trend Discovery website to find what’s been trending over the past 7, 30 and 120 days.

Hashtags play an essential role in TikTok’s algorithm.

They help determine what your content is about and how it should be ranked in relevant searches and For You pages.

By using popular hashtags related to your content, you increase the chances of appearing in searches for those specific topics or trends.

Using a mix of broad and niche hashtags will give your videos the best chance of ranking on TikTok.

Broad hashtags have the power to reach a wide range of users, increasing the chances of your content being discovered by new viewers.

These are often trending hashtags that are popular at the moment.

By including these in your posts, you can tap into larger trends and gain exposure to a broader audience.

On the other hand, niche hashtags attract people who are already interested in content similar to yours.

These tags allow you to target specific communities or topics within TikTok.

When users search for or follow these specific hashtags, they’re more likely to come across your TikTok videos if you use them strategically.

Incorporating relevant niche hashtags increases the visibility of your content among those who have a genuine interest in what you’re sharing.

Also, if you create location-specific content TikTok’s geological tags can be beneficial for you.

Using these tags and relevant local hashtags can land your videos on TikTok’s Nearby feed, reaching an audience interested in content from that area.

### Add Keywords & Hashtags to Your Account & Videos

To ensure that your videos are easily discoverable, it’s important to include the exact in the title, description, video cover, and even on-screen text like lyrics or explanations.

Additionally, don’t forget to say those specific keywords out loud at the start of the video as TikTok’s algorithms prioritise content where the keywords are spoken.

When using hashtags, make sure to include both your main keyword and any variations that make sense.

This will help people find your posts more easily when they search for related topics or TikTok trends.

However, it’s essential not to overdo it with hashtags. The optimal number of hashtags for each TikTok video is three to five.

Adding your most relevant target keywords to your TikTok profile can increase visibility when users search for those specific terms.

By doing so, you not only enhance the chances of attracting potential followers but also provide TikTok with an idea of what kind of content you post.

### Use TikTok Trending Audio

One quick trick to stay updated with the hottest trends is to open TikTok and search for “trending sounds”.

By filtering the videos to ‘this week’, you can find hot content that is currently trending.

Utilising trending audio not only keeps your TikTok content fresh and relevant but also boosts your visibility in TikTok search results.

TikTok’s Trend Discovery website also contains details of the latest trending songs.

Take a look through to give you some ideas of the songs that you can use to create videos.

Incorporating these trendy sounds into your videos enhances the chances of appearing in TikTok search engine results when users explore related content.

### Collaborate & Engage with other Creators

While not strictly Tiktok SEO, collaborating with other creators on TikTok is a powerful way to expand your reach.

When you collaborate with other creators, you tap into their audience base, exposing your content to a whole new set of viewers who may not have discovered you otherwise.

This increased exposure can lead to more engagement on your videos, such as likes, comments, and shares.

Engaging with other creators goes beyond just collaborating on TikTok videos.

It also involves interacting with their TikTok content by liking, commenting, and sharing it.

By engaging with other creators’ content, you not only show support for their work but also build relationships within the TikTok community.

This can lead to reciprocal engagement from those creators and their followers on your own content.

### Use Comments For Content Ideation

If a user posts a question or comment on your video then consider creating a Tiktok video in reply.

This works well as the chances are that more people will have the same query. So it not only provides a follow-up or clarification but gives you more ideas for relevant content.

It also encourages users to comment more on your videos which only increases your engagement.

TikTok SEO changes quickly so building a rapport with your followers is a great way of connecting with what your audience wants and discovering new trends as they happen.

### Encourage Interaction

Remember to use calls to action (CTAs) in your videos.

Remind people to interact with your videos in the comments. Some examples could be:

- Let me know your favourite in the comments!
- Comment below what you think…
- Post in the comments if you want to see part two

You’ll be surprised how verbalising this interaction encourages people to take action.

## TikTok Videos Ranking Factor

When it comes to TikTok ranking factors, there are three key points you need to focus on:

1. User interactions
2. Video information
3. Account settings

### User Interactions

The user interactions on TikTok play a key role in determining what content is shown to users on TikTok.

- Likes
- Shares
- Follows
- Comments
- Saved videos
- Viewer retention
- ‘Not interested’

This data is then used by TikTok’s algorithm to curate a tailored feed that showcases videos most likely to capture the specific users’ attention.

The significance of user interactions in TikTok SEO can’t be overstated.

The more engagement users have with certain types of content, the higher the chances that similar content will be recommended to them.

This is why creating quality content is so important.

Good Tiktok SEO can get your videos in front of a new audience, but if the videos aren’t worth watching then you won’t get the full benefits or new followers.

Remember to encourage viewers to interact with your content, especially when you’re a content creator.

It’s a great way to grow your audience and get individual videos into the algorithm.

### Video Information

To optimize your presence on TikTok, it’s crucial to provide relevant video information.

This includes captivating captions, trending hashtags, and catchy music.

Start by creating engaging and informative captions that accurately describe the content of your video.

This not only helps users understand what they can expect from your video but also provides valuable keywords for TikTok’s algorithm to recognise and rank your content.

Also, incorporate trending hashtags into your video information to greatly improve its discoverability.

Research popular hashtags related to the topic or theme of your video and include them strategically in your captions or comments section.

By doing so, you increase the chances of your videos appearing in relevant Tiktok search engine results or being featured on TikTok’s For You page.

### Account Settings

The account setting that a user has plays a role in the types of content that they see.

However, it has a lower weight compared to video information and user interactions.

- Language preferences
- Country location
- Android or iOS device
- Categories of interest

Keep in mind that while these account settings do contribute towards TikTok SEO ranking, they are not the sole determining factors for success on the platform.

So make sure to create high-quality content, optimize your profile, and stay consistent to increase your chances of success on TikTok.

## How Does the TikTok Search Engine Algorithm Work?

As you delve into the workings of the TikTok algorithm, you discover how it curates a personalised experience for each user.

This is based on their demographics, browsing history and interactions.

It begins when a user creates a TikTok account.

The app takes into account their age, pronouns, location (if allowed), and selected categories to show them relevant content.

As the user interacts with the app, TikTok will track this information.

Interactions include scrolling past content that doesn’t interest them and engaging with videos that appeal do appeal to them.

The algorithm then starts showing users more content similar to the videos that they liked and watched all the way through while filtering out content that doesn’t capture their attention.

Another factor TikTok uses is the cookies and browsing history on your device.

This means that it can further tailor your experience by considering web pages visited outside of the app.

The more engagement a user has with the app, the better it understands their interests and can deliver an optimized stream of entertainment.

This level of personalisation is what sets TikTok apart from other platforms as it consistently learns about its users’ preferences to provide an engaging experience.

## How to Find What’s Trending on TikTok

To find out what’s trending, there are several easy methods you can use.

### Videos

- **TikTok Creator Centre** : Find trending videos here
- **STITCH feature** : You can stitch your video onto the end of a relevant trend video and your content will then appear in the results when people search for the trend

### Music and Sounds

- **TokBoard** : A third-party website that provides weekly updates on the top trending songs. This site is one of the best options for quickly accessing the relevant songs that you should be using in your content.
- **TikTok Creator Centre** : Here you will find a list of the most popular songs of all time as well as breakout entries. By selecting ‘Breakout’, you can see which songs are currently trending. The advantage of using this method is that it also provides detailed analytics such as when a particular song started trending, audience demographics, location data, and related sounds.
- **For You Page** : Scrolling through your will give you a glimpse at the sounds that are most commonly used. By engaging with this content through likes and comments, TikTok will serve you similar content and more trending sounds based on your preferences.
- **Searching** : Simply type in ‘trending sounds’ or ‘viral sounds’ in the search bar and click on ‘sounds’

## Why Should You Optimize TikTok for SEO?

TikTok SEO helps the search algorithm find your content and connect it with the right people.

Putting your content in front of the right people is the number one way to start increasing your engagement and building a following.

When your content aligns with what users are searching for, it increases the likelihood of attracting viewers who find your content interesting and relevant.

TikTok SEO also enables you to optimize your TikTok video so that it appears in the For You pages of users who have shown an interest in similar content.

This means that even if users aren’t actively searching for specific keywords, there is still a chance for your videos to reach them.

TikTok shopping has been announced for the Australian market with integrations for WooCommerce, Shopify and other [eCommerce](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/ecommerce-seo-agency/) platforms. So it pays for brands to start building a bigger audience now. 

On top of that, Google can index and rank your videos if they’re optimized. So TikTok SEO goes hand in hand with started SEO content strategies.

By implementing a strong TikTok SEO strategy, you can create content that is tailored to the interests and preferences of your target audience.

By focusing on creating relevant content that resonates with your target audience, you increase the chances of viewers engaging with your videos through likes, comments, and shares.

This not only enhances user engagement but also improves the discoverability of your content among other users who share similar interests.

Ultimately, TikTok SEO allows you to be more intentional in reaching a highly targeted audience and building a strong brand presence on the platform.

## How is Tiktok SEO Different from Traditional SEO?

The biggest difference is that you are optimizing video content rather than pages of text.

While traditional SEO like Google search focuses on text-based content like articles and blog posts, TikTok SEO revolves around visual content in the form of videos.

This means that to optimize your TikTok account, you’ll need to focus on creating engaging and visually appealing videos that capture your audience’s attention.

Another key difference lies in the method of discovery.

In traditional SEO, keywords play a crucial role in helping users find relevant information.

While this is true also true on TikTok, you can elevate a standard keyword SEO strategy with the use of hashtags.

By using popular and relevant hashtags in your TikTok video captions and descriptions, you can increase its visibility and attract more viewers.

Each platform has different metrics and indicators for what they classify as successful content.

On TikTok, engagement metrics such as likes, comments, and shares are vital indicators of a video’s performance.

The more engagement your video receives, the higher its chances of reaching a wider audience.

Whereas, traditional SEO places greater emphasis on authority and [link building](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/link-building-agency-in-australia/) to rank high on search engine results pages.

## Type of Content That isn’t Recommended on TikTok

Avoid creating content that falls into certain specific categories, as TikTok’s recommendation systems may flag it and prevent it from reaching a wider audience.

It is crucial to adhere to the TikTok community guidelines when producing your videos.

If your content falls into the following categories then you might want to consider removing it.

**Duplicate content**: Videos that are identical or very similar in nature.**Spam conten**t: Videos that include unwanted advertising or deceptive practices.**Overly promotional**:  Videos that are excessively promotional or contain misleading information.**Safety concerns**: Videos that pose a threat to someone’s safety such as dangerous stunts can be flagged to avoid imitation.**Overtly sexualised content**: Videos that include explicit material or nudity are prohibited**Tobacco and alcohol products**: Videos promoting these items goes against the platform’s objective of fostering a positive user experience.

## What is TikTok SEO?

One key to getting more views on your videos is by using strategies that help your content show up in search results and get discovered by a wider audience.

This is where TikTok SEO comes into play.

TikTok SEO, or search engine optimization, refers to the tactics and techniques used to improve the visibility and ranking of your videos on TikTok’s search bar and the For You page.

By optimizing your content for specific keywords and search queries, you increase the chances of your videos appearing in relevant searches.

To make the most out of TikTok SEO, it’s important to understand how the platform’s algorithm works.

When users type a keyword or phrase in the search bar, TikTok looks for relevant videos based on factors like captions, hashtags, sounds used, and user interactions.

It also considers ‘For You’ search queries which are phrases related to what users have previously searched for or interacted with.

By including popular keywords and relevant hashtags in your captions, as well as using trending sounds you can increase your chances of appearing higher in search results.

Remember that TikTok SEO is not just about getting more views; it’s about reaching the right audience who will engage with and enjoy your content.

To see how our TikTok SEO agency can help grow your Tiktok, [send our team a message](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/contact/) and we’ll be in touch.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How can I increase my TikTok followers using SEO strategies?

To increase your TikTok followers using SEO strategies, focus on optimizing your profile and content. Use specific keywords in your bio, captions, and hashtags. Also, use trends to your advantage to increase the chances of your content appearing on the ‘For You’ page.

### Can I use keywords and hashtags to optimize my TikTok content?

Yes, you can definitely use keywords and hashtags to optimize your TikTok content. By strategically incorporating keywords and popular hashtags, you can increase the discoverability of your videos and attract more viewers and followers.

### Are there any specific tips for optimizing my TikTok profile for SEO?

To optimize your TikTok profile for SEO, focus on creating engaging content that resonates with your target audience. Research keywords to use in your bio and captions, and regularly engage with other users to increase your visibility.

### How important is the engagement rate in TikTok SEO?

The engagement rate is crucial for TikTok SEO. The platform’s algorithm prioritises content with high engagement, such as likes, comments, and shares. By increasing your engagement rate, you can boost visibility and reach on TikTok.

### Is it possible to track the performance of my TikTok SEO efforts?

Yes, it is possible to track the performance of your TikTok SEO efforts. You can use analytics tools provided by TikTok to monitor metrics such as views, likes, shares, and comments to evaluate the effectiveness of your optimization strategies.

## Essential Digital Marketing Terms

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/20-digital-marketing-terms-need-know/

### 20 Digital Marketing Terms You Need to Know

#### SEO

# 20 Digital Marketing Terms You Need to Know

1.  **GA: Google Analytics**

A service offered by Google that offers a detailed breakdown about a website’s traffic and traffic sources, while measuring conversions and sales. GA is an extremely useful tool to learn more about your audience and their behaviour on your website.

1. **[SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/): Search Engine Optimisation**

Refers to the practices and techniques that increase your website rank in organic search results, which ultimately improves the visibility of your website to people looking for your product, or service via search engines like Google, Bing, and Yahoo.

1. **CTA: Call-to-Action**

Any hyperlink, button, photo, or any other form of link that attempts to motivate a potential customer to carry out an action on your site, such as subscribing to your email list or signing up to your website.

1.  **PPC: Pay-per-Click**

An advertising model where the advertiser will pay the publisher a specific amount of money for every instance a visitor engages with an advertisement. When running advertisements on Google, Bing or Yahoo, PPC ads are displayed in a visible location (usually at the top of the results) based on their keyword list, which is given to the publisher before launching the PPC campaign.

1.  **SEM: Search Engine Marketing**

A form of Internet marketing that aims to boost the visibility of websites in search engine results pages (SERPs) through SEO and paid advertising.

1.  **USP: Unique Selling Position**

The term is used to refer to any characteristic of a product, service or business that distinguishes it from similar objects or services.

1.  **CPC: Cost-per-Click**

Refers to the exact cost to get a potential customer to engage with your digital advertisement. CPC allows you to measure the effectiveness and profitability of your campaign.

1.  **Clickthrough Rate (CTR)**

The amount of visitors that progresses (or clicks through) from one level of your marketing funnel to the next one. To calculate your CTA, divide the overall amount of hits that your webpage or CTA gets by the amount of options people are able to click.

1.  **Cost per Action (CPA)**

CPA refers to the exact amount spent for a specified action a user takes, such as a purchase, comment, like, or share. CPA is useful for determining how much you are spending for a desired action from your target audience.

1.  **CPL: Cost-per-Lead**

This is a crucial metric as it measures the exact amount it costs for your campaign to acquire a lead.

1.  **Bounce rate**

Bounce rate can be used in two different circumstance. Bounce rate on your website is the amount of visitors who view a webpage on your site who then exit without engaging with anything on the page or with your other webpages. The higher your bounce rate the more likely your visitors are not interested or engaged enough by your content to stay. Bounce rate for your emails refers to the rate an email does not reach the intended recipients inbox. If your email bounce rate is above average in this case suggests it that your email list is outdated or includes fake/invalid emails.

1.  **Conversion Rate (CR)**

Refer to the amount of visitors who carried out a specific action while viewing a certain web page e.g. making a purchase. As a general rule of thumb, the higher the conversion rate on a page the better, whereas pages with lacklustre CRs are not performing the best they can (although this doesn’t apply in all situations).

1.  **Search Engine Results Pages (SERPs)**

This is what you see when you look something up on a search engine such as Google. It refers to the listing of webpages returned by a search engine based on a specific keyword search.

1.  **Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)**

Refers to the strategies that aim to enhance your websites conversion rate through design practices, key customer experience principles, and of course testing. It focuses on building an experience that aims to convert your target audience into clients. CRO can also be applied to a specific web site or landing webpage, alternatively it can be applied in search engine marketing, social media advertising, and other channels of your advertising strategy.

1.  **ROAS: Return on Advertising Spend**

Calculating the ROAS allows online marketers to determine whether their advertising budget is generating sufficient revenue. To calculate ROAS, divide the revenue generated by a campaign or ad source by the advertising expenses.

1.  **A/B Testing** 

Also referred to as split testing, this is the process of comparing two variations of a single variation to determine which version performs better in order to optimise your marketing efforts. Some popular examples include email marketing (modifications to the subject line or copy), Landing Pages (with tweaks in content), and with Search Engine Marketing (testing two ads simultaneously to determine which receives a higher click through rate).

1.  **Customer Relationship Management (CRM)**

Refers to any computer programs that enables businesses record every single interaction they have with their customers. This includes activities like tracking emails, phone calls, sales; sending personalised messages; organising appointments; recording every interaction with customer service or [technical](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/technical-seo-agency/) support.

1.  **Keywords**

These are the crucial words or phrases that are relevant to your website and business. Keywords are the topics or ideas that webpages get indexed in search results by engines like Google, Yahoo, and Bing. When selecting keywords, you need to ensure the keyword you are targeting has a large search volume and is relevant to the audience you’re targeting. Keywords are integral components of both Search Engine Marketing (SEM) and Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Long-tail keywords are made up of a phrase that contains at least three words, and are more effective for targeting specific niche audiences.

1.  **UX (User Experience)**

User experience encompasses the complete experience a customer has with a business, including their discovery and awareness of the brand all the way through to their engagement, purchase behaviour, use of a service or product, and even their opinion of the product or service. To create a great customer experience, you need to empathise with your customer’s perspective. Consider what would add the most value for them from your product or service.

## Google Penalty Recovery Strategies

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/google-penalty-recovery-strategies/

### The Business Cost of Google Penalties and Recovery Strategies

#### SEO

# The Business Cost of Google Penalties and Recovery Strategies

Over the last three years we have been working with numerous clients in the Australian and global market to assist with penalty recovery – both Algorithmic and Manual penalties. The thing about Google Penalties is that they can result in a detrimental loss to business revenue if you are not quick to develop a recovery strategy.

I would like to talk to you about four different businesses who have been hit by penalties on the larger scale of things. I also want to talk over some strategies we have used to assist with regaining organic positioning and the overall loss to revenue for the business. For privacy reasons I cannot name the four businesses we have worked with.

**Business One:** Online Education Portal**Penalty:** Algorithm update.**Business loss** – $100,000 per month loss in organic search revenue.**Project Status:** Project complete.

**Business Two:** Global Crowd Source Website.**Penalty:** Manual Penalty.**Business loss:** Post $X million funding round saw traffic drop by 50%.**Project Status:** Project complete.

**Business Three:** Large US based Holiday portal**Penalty:** Algorithmic penalty**Business loss:**  50% loss in organic traffic, meaning $x million loss in revenue a year.**Project Status:** Project complete.

**Business Four:** Financial Portal**Penalty:** Manual & Algorithmic penalty**Business loss:** Investors dropped out of a $x million funding round after finding out about the penalty.**Project Status:** Underway

Now in all four cases listed above we did not complain to Google. Nor did we post on product forums or tech sites saying we were unfairly hit. We developed a recovery strategy and ongoing business plan for each specific company.

The three businesses above are all quite switched on from an [SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) point of view. Three of the businesses even have in-house SEO teams. The thing about Manual and Algorithmic penalties is that it is a highly specialized area of SEO. I find our company time and time again fixing up the poor quality work which other agencies have tried to implement recovery strategies on websites.

**Recovery Strategy** 

**Step 1 – Find out the history of the business.** 

Find out who was doing SEO for the business in the past 10 years. Try and recover any documentation which was sent. Usually just saying the name of the SEO company who has completed the past work provides an instant picture of the damage.

As an example, here are two so called “well known” Sydney based agencies and the damage they have caused to many businesses:

Example agency name one – Built a large scale link network which was struck hard by penguin update, resulting in many websites being hit hard.

Example agency name two – Built a large amount of article marketing robot spam. To gain quick results on exact match keywords they would spam 1000’s of articles. This resulted in many of their clients being hit hard by Manual penalties for non organic links.

**Step 2 – Collect all the data possible.**

Personally we like to use various data sources such as Link Risk, Ahrefs, Majestic SE and Google Webmaster Tools data.

I think the issue here is that many people who use tools like Link Research Tools take the lazy way out. They pull the report from LRT and instantly disavow 100’s of good links with no analysis.

**Step 3 – Complete analysis on the domains in question.**

You need to do deep analysis into the link profile which you are completing analysis on. The larger and more complex the link profile, the more research you will need to do. As an example, if there are multiple redirects to the domain and historic issues it could mean even more work from an analysis point of view.

**Step 4 – Complete manual link removal on the domain.**Once you have completed a comprehensive link analysis on the domain you need to manually remove a number of domains.

**Step 5 – Complete a comprehensive disavow file.**

When making a disavow file you need to ensure that you are 100% sure you want to add the links. Also ensure that you block domains using the root URL. Numerous times on analysis of disavow files we have noticed raw URL’s been used, or even the wrong formatting used in the disavow files. Another common problem we have noticed is that businesses rely to heavily on Link Research Tools and often end up disavowing a large number of “good domains”.  

**Step 6 – Work out your next steps.**

Will you be doing a reconsideration request if it is a manual penalty. If it an algorithmic penalty you will be unable to submit a reconsideration request. With manual penalties it may involve several attempts to re gain positioning.

**Step 7 – Work out if you need to do on going link building to make the link profile more natural.**For most domains which have been hit by low quality link building you need to complete fresh link building to balance the link profile. This may involve using high quality link building strategies to target subcategory sections of the site and to build more branded and URL based links.

**Step 8 – Repeat the process and keep doing analysis on work.**Repeat the analysis process on the domain and check on on going process, ideally you need to be looking at segments such as:

- Organic traffic analysis on a month by month comparison.
- Organic lead generation comparison.
- Search visibility analysis.
- Large scale keyword analysis on an on going basis to look for ranking fluctuations.Additional reading (Penalty Recovery Strategy on Power Retail – [http://www.powerretail.com.au/marketing/how-to-recover-from-a-google-penguin-penalty/](http://www.powerretail.com.au/marketing/how-to-recover-from-a-google-penguin-penalty/) )

**Results from on going Penalty Recovery Work –** 

**Business 1** – Online Education Portal

For the Online Education Portal we removed a large amount of low quality links & completed a comprehensive disavow file.

A full case study here for this recovery project can be found here – [http://moz.com/ugc/increasing-organic-seo-traffic-by-400000-unique-visitors-a-month](http://moz.com/ugc/increasing-organic-seo-traffic-by-400000-unique-visitors-a-month)

**Business 2 –** Global Crowd Source Website.

[As we can see from the Crowd sourcing website organic visibility is increasing, the business invests heavily on PPC and has a large budget to do so.](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/crowd-funding.jpg)

**Business 3** – Large US based Holiday portal

This large holiday portal contacted our business in March 2013 for assistance with a Penalty Recovery, the website had been hit hard by an algorithmic penalty. We were successful in recovery around mid 2013, further to this we assisted the client with a new strategy and direction for on going link building. The business has moved from strength to strength. 

**Business 4 –** Financial Portal

This is a recent project we are assisting with, the website was hit heavily by a manual penalty which then followed with a algorithmic penalty in the most recent update as we can see the traffic loss for the website is quite heavy from an organic visibility point of view.


As we can see their is a recovery strategy for all websites online for some it just takes far longer than others. Penalty analysis time can take 1-2 months and recovery can take upwards of 6 months. In addition to this some project may take longer and 100% recovery can never be guaranteed. Also please not the data from SEM Rush is to be used as a guide/ estimation only.

If you need assistance with a [enterprise](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/) level Google penalty recovery or a mid level project feel free to contact Prosperity Media today, we will be happy to provide expertise and assistance on recovery.

## Benefits of Enterprise SEO

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/what-are-the-benefits-of-enterprise-seo/

### What are the Benefits of Enterprise SEO?

# What are the Benefits of Enterprise SEO?

With over a decade of experience as an [enterprise SEO company](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/), we’ve successfully partnered with leading brands across Australia, Europe and the U.S. This means we know the challenges large-scale websites face and how much of a difference SEO can make. 

We’ll explore the key benefits of [enterprise SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/) so you can create a business case to justify the marketing spend.

## What is Enterprise SEO?

Enterprise [SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) is the comprehensive, strategic approach to optimising large-scale websites for search engines. 

Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on smaller websites or niche markets, enterprise SEO manages and optimises websites with thousands of pages, complex structures and multiple pages.

## Key Benefits of Enterprise SEO

Understanding the benefits makes it easier to communicate to decision-makers why SEO should be a priority. This can give more weight to your argument when building your annual budget.

1. Scalability in SEO Strategies

A core benefit of enterprise SEO efforts is scalability. Large websites with thousands of pages require a scalable SEO solution to manage and optimise content efficiently across various domains and platforms.

Whether updating existing content, expanding into different markets or launching new products, enterprise SEO offers the tools and strategies to handle the scale. It ensures pages are optimised properly without sacrificing quality.

1. Improved [Technical](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/technical-seo-agency/) SEO

There are so many moving for technical SEO for enterprises. From optimising page speed and fixing crawl issues to managing site architecture and addressing indexing problems. It’s important to maintain health and performance for sites of this size.

Fixing and improving these issues makes your site quicker, reduces crawl budget, and better promotes important content. All of these things are ranking factors and helps to increase revenue. A strong technical foundation also improves user experiences, boosting engagement and conversions.

1. Data-Driven Decision Making

In enterprise SEO, decisions aren’t based on guesswork. Data powers them from Google Analytics, Google Search Console and other relevant platforms. Advanced analytics and big data play a significant role in shaping SEO strategies for large enterprises.

We analyse traffic patterns, user behaviour, keyword performance, and conversion metrics to make informed decisions for clients. This leads to better outcomes becomes you have a better understanding of your market and customer interactions. Data-driven insights allow you to identify areas for growth, refine your targeting strategies and maximise ROI.

1. Overall Marketing Strategy Integration

Enterprise website SEO integrates seamlessly with broader marketing strategies. This ensures SEO and your wider marketing goals remain consistent across all digital channels. The integration allows our clients to execute cohesive campaigns that enhance brand visibility, strengthen customer engagement and drive targeted traffic.

Enterprise SEO works in concert with other digital marketing initiatives, including paid media, content marketing and social media, to achieve business goals in a unified way.

1. Enterprise-Level Content Strategy

Developing an enterprise content strategy aligns content creation and optimisation with larger business objectives.

The volume of content can be overwhelming for large-scale websites. Enterprise SEO provides a framework to manage it effectively, including creating high-quality content relevant to your target audience and meeting user and search engine expectations.

A content strategy improves organic visibility, attracts qualified traffic, and strengthens a brand’s digital presence when executed well.

1. Competitive Edge Through Advanced Tools

To stay competitive, enterprise businesses must leverage advanced [SEO tools](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo-tools/) and platforms. These tools can provide insights into:

- Market trends
- Competitor performance
- Keyword opportunities
- Technical issues

With technology, we automate routine tasks, conduct in-depth analysis and implement sophisticated strategies, giving our enterprise clients a competitive edge.

1. Enhanced Brand Authority and Visibility

A robust enterprise SEO strategy enhances brand authority and visibility and improves search rankings for enterprise sites.

As your business consistently appears at the top of search results for relevant keywords, your brand’s credibility grows, increasing trust among your target audience.

Benefits of this improved authority can include:

- A solidified position as a market leader.
- Better customer engagement.
- Improved brand loyalty.
- More qualified traffic and higher conversion rates.
- Long-term growth.

### Understanding Enterprise SEO Strategies

Enterprise SEO tactics include a wide range of skills, in addition to keyword research, [link building](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/link-building-agency-in-australia/), and other fundamental search engine optimisation elements. These can include

- Advanced technical SEO
- Scalable content strategies
- The integration of SEO with broader marketing initiatives
- Deep data analysis
- Sophisticated keyword targeting
- The use of leading-edge tools

The goal isn’t just improving search engine rankings—it’s to ensure a cohesive, brand-aligned digital presence across all markets and platforms.

### How Enterprise SEO Differs from Traditional SEO

The key difference between enterprise SEO and traditional SEO lies in the scale and complexity of operations. Enterprise SEO requires a more holistic approach. It addresses the unique challenges of managing vast amounts of content and consistency across multiple markets.

Enterprise SEO needs to align with overall business strategies.

There’s also a high level of coordination among teams, including IT, marketing and content. Traditional SEO, on the other hand, usually focuses on smaller websites with fewer pages, so execution is less complex and more straightforward.

## Challenges of Enterprise SEO

Enterprise SEO has enormous benefits but also comes with its own set of challenges. Working with enterprise SEO teams that understand these challenges is critical to proactively developing effective strategies to address them.

### Complexity of Implementation

Among the main challenges enterprise SEO faces is the management of complex situations. Enterprise-level websites have multiple stakeholders. These include:

- IT
- Marketing
- Content teams
- External vendors

Each has its priorities and objectives. Coordinating the efforts can lead to bottlenecks and delays.

Additionally, the structure of large websites adds another layer of complexity.

We understand that successfully navigating this environment requires clear communication, robust project management and a strategic approach that aligns all parties toward a shared goal.

### Keeping Up with Algorithm Updates

Search engine algorithms change constantly. Staying ahead of these changes is an ongoing enterprise SEO challenge.

SEO algorithm updates can significantly impact the visibility and ranking of large sites, especially if they’re addressed promptly.

The stakes are higher for an enterprise because of the scale of operations.

With that in mind, we take a proactive approach to monitoring and adapting to these updates. This involves:

- Regularly auditing the website.
- Staying informed about the latest SEO trends.
- Implementing necessary adjustments to ensure your site complies with search engine guidelines and best practices.

### Maintaining Consistency Across Global Markets

Enterprises operating across multiple regions face the challenge of maintaining consistent SEO performance. A global SEO strategy needs to account for:

- Different languages.
- Cultural nuances.
- Local search behaviours.
- Varying levels of competition in each market.

Ensuring consistency across these diverse regions requires a tailored approach balancing global objectives and local optimisation efforts. Some of the strategies we use to address these challenges include:

- Creating region-specific content and web pages.
- Implementing localised keyword strategies.
- Adapting technical SEO elements.

Our goal is always to achieve uniform brand visibility and user experience worldwide, considering each target market’s unique characteristics.

## Dental SEO Expertise

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/dental-seo-expert/

### Dental SEO Expert

# Dental SEO Expert

**Prosperity Media has over 12 years of experience working with Dental Clients in the Australian and NZ markets.**

**We understand the your goal as a dentist is to keep your chairs booked and your phone ringing.**

The goal as a dentist, is to rank well for all local queries in your given market and rank well in Google Business Listings.

As the director of Prosperity Media, my wife is a dentist so we understand the market.

We have worked with clients such as Putney Dental, Australian Dental Specialists, and many others to ensure they dominate their given markets.

Project pricing starts at $3,000 + GST a month for Dental SEO.

**Quick Insights**

**Is local SEO different from SEO?**

Local SEO is a specific set of tactics and techniques to improve your dental practice’s online presence to your service area. It often involves optimising your Google My Business listing(s) for localised dentistry-related searches.

**Can you do your own dental [SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/)?**

There’s nothing stopping you from carrying out your own on-page and off-site SEO. In fact, in this article, we’ll share a few process that you can replicate in your own time.

## How Search Engine Optimisation Can Solve Your Problem

You didn’t invest 7 years of your life into becoming a dentist and tens of thousands of dollars into your dental practice just to worry about the lack of new patients.

But not all SEO companies are the same. Read on to see why we are dental SEO experts.

**Dental SEO**

Search Engine Optimization (SEO) can be key for any dental practice to get ahead in the digital sphere. For an industry that often relies on traditional marketing and word of mouth, the foot traffic potential from the online channels can sometimes be pushed to the back. Think of how many things you Google; businesses, cafes, restaurants, research papers, ‘near me’. As a dentist, SEO can be very critical to your digital marketing plan, essentially so that your website ranks first, on the first page, as an organic search result.

__But What Is Dental SEO?__

SEO refers to the optimisation of search engines as part of a digital marketing strategy. Google and similar search engines have algorithms put in place which rank websites in terms of relevancy and popularity for your search term. Their ‘bots’ will crawl through sites in accordance with this algorithm to rank your site, and ultimately, if your website is not near the top on the first place, there is a high chance it will be missed by potential customers. Luckily, these search engine rankings can be influenced through a variety of optimisation techniques, so that your online presence is built high and potential patients can find your dental practice. The following are four pillars of SEO, which each present some of the key areas for optimisation:

__1.__ __Content Marketing__

Content Marketing involves the creation of online material that does not explicitly promote the brand, rather revolves around creating value and customer relationships by understanding consumer interests and needs. This online material, which may take the form of a blog or onsite content, indirectly drives people to the product.

**Keyword Research****–** 

Tools and software are used to determine what dental terms, phrases and questions are being searched for regarding a particular keyword. These can be used when building and reviving current websites, or writing content about that keyword, as the most searched results help understand what the consumer cares about. These keywords may be short-tail (one to two words and straight to the point), or longtail (a more specific, long question-like search). For Dental, an example of short-tail search would be ‘retainer’, whereas a longtail could be ‘how often are you supposed to clean a retainer?’. Keywords and their relevant terms can be incorporated into articles, blogs and other content which is picked up by the search engine crawl bots, and thus allows the dental site to achieve topical relevancy which gives the content a greater probability to rank higher in the SERPs.

**Content Analysis- Pruning** 

For your dental website, there may be many pages, but not all of them have value. Content Pruning is when the pages on your site are redundant, and you remove or improve those that have little traffic or value. The pages that weigh down a website will no longer be crawled by bots, and the overall performance of the site will improve, thus placing your clinic website higher on the search ranking page. Other things to consider include bounce rates, traffic, time spent on page & interaction.

**Content Analysis – Onsite Optimisation** 

Onsite Optimisation revolves around ensuring titles, tags, photos and the written content on your dental website are optimised to targeted keywords and searched terms. It is also very important to update old content with new relevant information, as content freshness is a ranking factor with all other things being equal (called Query Deserves Freshness or QDF for short). This on-page content optimisation can ensure the phrases and information given is what potential clients are searching for.

__2. Link Building__ 

Essentially, links are like votes for your dental site. The more links you have, the more Google believes your site is of high quality as it is being cited often. SEO specialists incorporate [link building](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/link-building-agency-in-australia/) to help dental services thrive online.

**Outreach and Authoritative Blogs**

Outreach is the process of prospecting relevant and well-known sites, obtaining an email and writing to them to pitch an article. The article may be an updated version of something they have written in the past, or new relevant content. Within the pitched article, there would be a link back to your Dental site, and perhaps other sites to show authenticity. Once this link is published on authoritative dental sites and blogs, Google will see the site is worthy of citation, and thus be boosted on the search engine ranking. Blogs are usually centred around a list to make it engaging and easy to digest by the reader, such as ‘Top 5 Best Tips for Braces’.

[PR](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/digital-pr-agency/) Links 

Being linked back to in an externally written article also builds up links. This is usually undertaken through PR, guest posts, and journalists outreaching for a source to cite. For example, if a journal of dentistry or health online magazine wanted insight from dentists, your dental clinic could submit a line, with your name and a link to your dental clinic website.

**Quora and Yahoo Answers** 

Quora and Yahoo Answers are other ways to boost your organic search ranking, without being too self-promotional. Answering questions allows for engagement within the community, and if you help solve an issue, the dental clinic you recommend becomes more memorable. This work particularly well for long-tail keywords.

__3.__ __Local SEO__

Local SEO is highly relevant in the dental industry, as usually, individuals will go to a dentist within close proximity to their house or workplace. Local SEO involves targeting those in the same geographic region and making your business website available to them at the time they need them. It is sometimes conducted through ‘near me’ searches, but regardless, search results will change depending on your specific location. This is because Google recognises some searches have ‘local intent’ such as dentist surgeries. For example, ‘How to clean a retainer’ does not have local intent as ‘best dentist near me’ does.

**Google My Business** **(GMB)**

Google my business is when Google takes searches a step further by providing a list on the results page of local businesses, a phone number, opening times, reviews and photos. They are increasingly becoming more sophisticated and may be general, such as listing multiple dentists in the area, or specific to one particular dental business.

**Local Citations** 

Local citations are mentions of the dental business on local business directories, community pages and social media platforms. Citations that are also geographically limited by industries such as professional services of dental directories are ideal for local dentists. This can assist the local web presence of the brand to consumers, resulting in new patients from the area, with the flow on benefit of improving local search rankings.

**4. [Technical](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/technical-seo-agency/) SEO**

This pillar of SEO is usually best left to the SEO experts, as the strategy becomes more advanced and tech-based.

**Website Speed**

Your Dental website’s site speed and page speed will be a big factor in Google’s ranking algorithm, as has come out and stated website speed in a ranking factor. It also betters the user experience when they come to fast running, professional looking dental site. Small changes can be made to improve this such as still incorporating photos which are compressed in size. Other changes are more advanced, such as where your site is hosted and what scripts your site is using.

**Site Architecture** 

Common structures that make up a page include HTML (the text of the site), CSS (the colours, fonts and looks of the site) and JavaScript (the interactive behaviour & frontend functions of the website). Your dental website will have a title, subpages, page templates and menu silos that will fall under these site architecture examples, whereby Google determines the quality and relevancy of these elements in their ranking. A relevant, readable URL and subsequent subpage URLs should be available for web users and bots to easily identify the purpose of the page.

**Schema** 

Incorporating a Schema markup is essentially manually enhancing the search result by adding features through codes. Aspects such as the dental practice’s review rating, local business schema using the Dentist markup.

__What should a Dental Practice Care About SEO Strategies?__

Dental Practices should strongly consider incorporating SEO into their marketing strategy to boost their organic search. Due to the popularity of the industry, local competition and a push to online tactics, SEO marketing is a significant factor in driving exposure and foot traffic. New dental patients can result from this online marketing technique when undertaken properly, through sincere content, links and local searches. Talk to an SEO expert today to better understand your options for optimisation.

## Local SEO Marketing Tips

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/local-seo-tips/

### Local SEO Tips

# Local SEO Tips

Whether you are a small business, a well-established player in your niche or a large franchisee, Local SEO marketing is an important tool to utilise to improve your online engagement.

In the past, the only way to get exposure and attract local customers would have been through a business directory like the Yellow Pages or your local paper. Although these traditional means of initial exposure may seem intuitive, now, Local SEO should be just as high on your priority list.

On average, 89% of people use their mobile or smartphone’s Google search function to look for local businesses at least once every week. Of this, 58% of people search for where a local coffee shop or convenience store is daily. That means that the pressure for every small business to have their Local [SEO](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) in check is slowly mounting. If your Local SEO isn’t optimised, you’re missing out on opportunities from local searches no matter how good your coffee tastes or what your shop is selling.

Knowing this can be really daunting but to help you out, we have decided to share a short guide on Local SEO to give you some SEO tips from our perspective.

## What is Local SEO?

Local search engine optimisation is a powerful tool used to increase the online visibility of your small business using local links and Google’s local functions. But, what is it?

The thing is, local search is still SEO – it requires keyword research, content, links, and on-page [technical](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/technical-seo-agency/) SEO. It is referred to as “local” because it has a geographic area focus to target people in the local community rather than the broader population. Basically, local SEO puts the focus on your local customers and tourists rather than people outside your geographical area.

Local information searches make up 46% of Google searches which means if you want to stay relevant in your local market you need to hop on the local search bandwagon. If you haven’t optimised your online presence for local search you’re already losing potential customers to your competition.

Therefore, the point of Local SEO is for people in your area to find your product or service first using Google search. To achieve this, you obviously need to rank highly in the search engine result pages (SERPs), specifically local results. This will also boost your online relevance geographically so you can build your following in your immediate proximity.

So, where do we get started? According to Moz’s Local SEO report, you should be focusing your Local SEO efforts on the top ranking factors, proximity and local keywords. It’s clear that when people look for local content they use specific location-based queries to find what they’re looking for but how does that help us?

Google has found that the most common local search queries are:

1. “Who’s close to me?”
2. “When are they open?”

This is where local SEO becomes really important. Making sure your online presence has accurate and up-to-date information including your working hours, address and business name all relate to your search ranking.

The phrase “near me today/tonight” has also seen an extremely dramatic increase from 2017 to 2019 as Google has now begun providing enhanced results for geographically related searches to meet their users’ needs.

These enhanced results are now based on:

- Proximity
- Relevance
- Prominence

Okay, but what does this mean? If a searcher is looking for a specific type of business they will be ranked on the proximity, relevance and prominence within the geographical location. This gives you no excuse to get onto your local SEO to make sure no one misses the opportunity to see your business online.

However, a surprising number of small businesses still lack a high-quality online presence that is location-specific for relevant local prospects. Local SEO is just like an online billboard or ad in the local paper. This style of on-site content marketing and backlinks can drive potential customers.

Still not convinced? Here are some of the benefits of implementing a local SEO strategy.

## What are the benefits of Local SEO Strategy?

Now you might be wondering why you should use Local SEO.

Over the years, ‘local intent’ has increased meaning that potential customers are searching for services within your local service area. There is no point in a Sydney café ranking high in Melbourne’s local search results, so it is imperative to improve your Local SEO if you want to increase your organic results. To capitalise on this, you can boost your Local SEO and your business will be the one they find at the top of local search rankings.

A successful Local SEO campaign will help your business because it:

- Pushes your local site up Google’s algorithm rankings and inserts it into the local pack.
- Is cost-effective for marketers and receives the highest level of conversion across all local advertising channels by using tools like Google My Business and Facebook.
- Increases online visibility, online presence, and organic traffic to your local site.
- Helps local customers find you via local search results, Google Maps or other navigational apps.
- Easily converts customers using mobile devices to convert sales almost instantly whether in search engines, through directories, or through social media channels.

It is important to be in both organic search and what Google calls the ‘Snack Pack’ of local listings as they make up 33% and 40% of clicks from potential leads. The first step in attempting to implement local SEO is therefore ensuring the optimisation of your local site across all channels.

## Step 1 – Ensure Your Website Is Optimised For All Channels

A good quality base of operations, like your website or Facebook page, is key to your small business ranking high. Ensuring that your site has a low load time, quality local content and is readable across all platforms will assist in your SEO rankings.

Customers are also more likely to contact a local business via mobile searches as the ease of searching on the go for local businesses is becoming more popular. Ensuring your website has mobile accessibility and simple navigation on all devices will ensure your site gets high priority.

## Step 2 – Claim and Optimise your Google My Business Listing

This is considered the most important part of Local SEO. Creating your Google My Business Listing gives potential customers easy access to your online presence including your business name, address (if you have a physical location), phone number and website.

More than just creating your online business profile, you should also add your foundational content including backlinks to important aspects of your website and your operating hours. Adding these additional resources for consumers will not only create a more user-friendly experience but will push you up in the results pages.

## Step 3 – Keyword Research

Implementing traditional SEO techniques is one of the best ways for your small business to rank well in local searches. Ensuring that your NAP is accurate and correlates across your all online platforms is your first step.

Brainstorming SiL’s (Service in Locations) should be your next step. By looking into your location and industry/niche you should be able to come up with some local keywords that will help you rank.

Google autocomplete is also a quick way to see what people are looking for in your area and to see what local keywords your competitors are looking for. Browsing local certified sites is another way to identify keywords your competitors may not have thought of.

## Step 4 – On-Page SEO Strategy

Enlisting in the help of On-Page SEO services should be your next step. There are a few things that you can do to enhance your on-site SEO.

One advancement you can make is utilising keywords in your H1, title tags, URL and meta description and including your NAP on your homepage to rank effectively. Using use testimonials or reviews on your website will also raise your online brand’s ethos.

Schema markup is also another way to improve the way that search engines read and represent pages in SERPs. To do this, employ Google Structure Data Markup Helper for tagging specific parts of your website including your NAP, title and other keywords.

Lastly, implementing an SEO [audit](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-audits/) and researching local landing pages and location directories to round out your SEO strategy.

## Step 5 – Building Local Citations and Local Links

There are two ways to build local citations, structured and unstructured.

Structured utilises mentions that include NAP information for business directories and social profiles. Unstructured involves creating local links through blog posts and preferred vendors to raise site rank and authority.

According to Moz, citations are one of the top local ranking factors for the Google ‘Snack Pack’ and organic search results. Consistent NAP information via citations and local links also contribute to rankings where inconsistency can confuse potential customers and Google. However, ensuring that these backlinks, content links and citations are of a high quality is extremely important.

## Step 6 – Quality Editorial Links via Link Building

Creating quality links through editorial content and [link building](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/link-building-agency-in-australia/) great affects localised organic rankings when targeting specific, niche blogs and sites.

Whether the content is on-site or on other sites, ensuring that you’re creating a useful resource rather than promoting a product or service directly will engage your potential leads. Consumers want to learn and seek out information like guides, recipes or how-to’s.

Quality content is of the utmost importance for the service industry specifically as people will be attracted to hiring professionals who are interested in helping them. The best way to find places to insert your editorial pieces is to look for local ‘write for us’ pages by looking up your local cities.

## Step 7 – Ongoing Maintenance

It also important to maintain and document your citations while link building with business associations, niche blogs and business directories.

There are three important, regular tasks that you need to review.

1. Online Customer Service: consistently responding to customers positive reviews and negative reviews

2. Inaccurate Google My Business Listings: sometimes, business listings are edited without notice to you or the business owner meaning that information may be inaccurate. Your job to make sure your information and citations are up to date at all times.

3. Use google posts to keep people up to date on-page.

## Summary

We covered the Local SEO, the benefits for a marketer, and what we know from an SEO and digital marketing perspective.

If you found this article useful please give it a share or contact our team to learn more.

## **B2B SEO Agency Services**

### **Technical SEO for Search Engines**

We use industry-standard tools to mimic search engine behaviour when crawling your site.

We speak developer, which just means we’re as nerdy and tech-savvy as your dev team.

Another crucial aspect of the technical audit is backlink analysis.

We would assess the quality and relevance of external websites linking back to yours.

This evaluation helps identify toxic or spammy backlinks that may harm your reputation with search engines.

Technical SEO improvements involve addressing issues like site speed optimization by compressing images or enabling browser caching.

Auditing URL canonicals ensure there are no duplicate content problems caused by multiple URLs pointing to the same page.

Mobile optimization is also a key component of a technical SEO audit since mobile-friendliness has become increasingly important for user experience and search engine rankings.

Our agency would examine if your website is responsive across different devices and screen sizes.

**Our B2B Client Examples**
