This could be in the form of insightful blog posts, whitepapers, or case studies that provide unique value to your target audience.

Additionally, actively seeking out opportunities for guest blogging on reputable industry websites can help expand your reach and establish credibility within your niche.

## **What is B2B Search Engine Optimization?**

Business-to-Business SEO is a strategy that aims to generate higher rankings and therefore more traffic.

B2B search engine optimization puts a business’ website above competitors to attract customers looking for their products and services.

Organic search can be divided into 3 main categories.

Here’s the top-level overview:

### **On-Page SEO for Organic Traffic**

Each landing page on your website should serve a purpose to either sell or inform your customers.

This is where On-Page SEO comes in and you have complete control.

On-Page SEO is having the perfect harmony of content for humans and keywords for robots.

When I mean robots, I’m talking about search engines such as Google, Bing and Yahoo.

A landing page that is just optimized for an algorithm with a poor user experience will give you a poor conversion rate.

And a perfectly crafted sales page with no optimization could convert but probably won’t receive much traffic from Google.

Just like a business starts with a set of ideas, every B2B SEO campaign starts with a set of keywords. The trick is choosing the correct ones.

You’ll want to choose keywords with low competition but high commercial value.

In many B2B niches, like marketing, keywords with low competition and high commercial value are scarce.

After years of experience, we’ve perfected our keyword research processes.

Schedule a call and we can help pinpoint the keywords that will get you the best ROI.

### **Off-Page**

Unlike On-Page SEO, Off-page is much harder to control.

Off-Page SEO is the process of earning a link from other websites to yours. The industry commonly refers to it as Backlinks or Link Building.

These are incredibly important when it comes to ranking for your target keywords and are often difficult to earn.

You can think of backlinks like votes. The more you have the better your rankings, organic traffic and visibility.

But it isn’t so much about quantity as it is quality. Otherwise, what’s stopping every marketer from going on Fiverr and paying for a $5 link blast?

If you want the best results, you’ll need to do outreach.

That means creating prospect lists, finding email addresses, crafting templates and sending messages.

You’ll also need to pay for SEO tools such as Ahrefs and Semrush.

Sure, it’s time-consuming and laborious but it’s a necessary evil.

We recommend you outsource it. Feel free to contact us.

We’ve been developing our outreach processes for years and earning our clients quality backlinks consistently each month.

### **Technical SEO**

Technical SEO is the process of optimizing your website for crawling and indexing.

Before Google can rank a page, they need to find your pages and store them.

If your site isn’t optimized for this, it may take longer to rank or if there are serious issues searchers may not see your pages in Google at all.

Those are the main concepts but lead generation for B2B SEO and B2C SEO are actually quite different.

## **Why is SEO Important for B2B Companies?**

If you’re running a B2B company, SEO is crucial for attracting potential customers who are already searching for your products or services online.

Great B2B SEO can give you a leg up on the competition and put you in front of decision-makers during their research process.

Implementing effective B2B SEO practices can have a significant impact on lead generation by increasing organic traffic and visibility.

By optimizing your website with relevant keywords, creating informative and valuable content, and improving user experience, you can attract qualified prospects.

Over time, search engine optimization will help to build your website’s authority. This makes it easier for your future content to rank and delivers sustainable, cost-effective results.

Also, measuring the ROI of your B2B SEO campaigns will help you to determine the effectiveness of your digital marketing campaigns.

By tracking metrics such as organic search traffic, conversion rates, and revenue generated from organic leads, you can evaluate the success of your SEO efforts and make data-driven decisions to optimize future campaigns.

## **Difference Between B2B SEO vs. B2C SEO**

There are some key differences between B2B and B2C SEO.

Knowing the difference between the two is paramount to the success of your B2B SEO strategies.

That’s why you need to partner with someone who is experienced in the industry.

### **Low Search Volumes**

B2B keywords have less search volume than B2C keywords. However, don’t let low search volumes discourage you.

If your customer lifetime value is high, then just 10 visitors per month could lead to one sale.

Search volumes may be lower but the amount of revenue per customer could be worth thousands of dollars.

Another issue is if your idea is too new or isn’t well established in the market, people won’t know how to search for it.

In order for SEO to be effective, there has to be search demand for your product or service.

### **B2B Requires More Nurturing**

In the case of DSLR cameras, consumers have no problem visiting the site and making a purchase on the spot.

“Food Photographer Sydney”, isn’t going to be as easy.

Ranking for this term has the potential to bring in huge revenue for the photography business but requires more lead nurturing.

Restaurant owners and catering companies are going to have questions about the services.

They’ll want to know what makes you different from the competition.

They might ask for more credentials and experience. In order to make a sale, you’ll typically need to follow up.

A high-ticket product or service naturally requires more research for both B2B and B2C.

The main difference is a B2B product or service is typically a lot more expensive to purchase and is a more long-term decision.

Whoever found you through Google may need to conduct more research, ask their boss about the budget or consult with their internal sales team before making a final verdict.

### **Online Reputation & Reviews**

In a B2C climate, businesses have the opportunity to do a high volume of sales through SEO.

That means more chances to nail the customer experience and get more positive reviews. If you receive negative feedback, you can easily dilute it.

In B2B, reputation is equally as important but the velocity of customers coming in is much slower.

You’ll need to make sure your online reputation is on point from day one.

That means asking your customers to leave a positive review the moment they’ve indicated they are satisfied with your product or service.

If your business has a poor reputation online, that will surely affect sales.

Customers won’t even consider your product or service if they see others talking about how it fails to meet expectations.

This area of SEO is called online reputation management.

## **What’s Working For B2B SEO Now?**

B2B SEO is getting more competitive year after year.

Authority sites, like Hubspot, are building up their domain authority using linkbait.

Domain authority makes it much easier to rank for lucrative keywords in your niche.

We’ve seen some powerful content marketing strategies and link magnets to help build the authority of B2B companies.

Contact us if you want some ideas of similar things we can create together as part of your B2B SEO strategy.

Here are some examples:

### **Tools**

Tools can be a great way to attract links and address the pain points of a certain target audience in your industry.

### **Design**

Canva created a tool that helps you choose one font and then find the ultimate pairing.

Canva has B2B and also B2C customers. The main appeal of this tool is that it solves a problem for web and graphic designers.

When creating a new design for a website or brand, there are hours spent on pairing fonts together.

This tool helps you do that in seconds.

Not only did it earn them 647 links, but also more brand recognition as it was highly shareable.

### **Marketing**

Co-Schedule created a headline analyzer: [https://coschedule.com/headline-analyzer](https://coschedule.com/headline-analyzer)

Co-Schedules’ ideal customer base is internal marketing teams.

Marketing teams need to come up with clickbait headlines for social media platforms in order to receive good engagement.

Naturally, it became wildly popular scoring 5,380 backlinks.

### **Content That Targets Specific Problems for custom ICP in B2B.**

Kinsta is a web hosting company that executes this strategy perfectly.

They know their customers’ pain points and have created keyword-targeted pages that solve their issues.

The upsell is their product but the main objective of this style of content is to increase brand recognition, awareness and attract links.

### **Statistics Pieces in B2B space**

At Prosperity Media, we’ve taken full advantage of this style of content for ourselves as well as our clients.

We created an [internet statistics](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/australian-internet-statistics/) piece that over time has earned us passive links. 

The entire concept is that journalists are looking for facts in your industry.

The first thing they do is check Google search engine results and then cite the top blog posts.

## Enterprise SEO Analytics Overview

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/understanding-enterprise-seo-analytics/

# Understanding Enterprise SEO Analytics

Managing SEO for large-scale organisations means high stakes and many intricacies. As experts in enterprise SEO, we’ve seen firsthand how critical it is to have robust analytics in place to drive success.

Enterprise SEO analytics is more than tracking keywords or monitoring traffic. It relies on understanding the full scope of your digital presence, interpreting complex data sets and making informed decisions in alignment with larger business goals. We’ll share our approach to analytics from an [enterprise SEO agency](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/). 

## What Analytics Tools Are Needed for Enterprise SEO?

When managing enterprise-level SEO, having the right tools available isn’t negotiable. The complexity and scale of the data require robust, reliable and versatile tools to provide insights that fuel informed decisions.

We’ll give a quick rundown of some of the enterprise SEO tools we use and recommend:

- [Google Analytics](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/) is the cornerstone of an SEO strategy. It provides insight into behaviour, traffic sources and conversion tracking. SEO reporting techniques are needed to segment data across multiple domains, understand user interactions at scale, and identify optimisation opportunities.
- [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about) lets you monitor your site’s presence in Google Search results. Managing large amounts of content at the enterprise level is valuable to ensure optimal performance for every page.
- [Screaming Frog](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/seo-spider/) is a tool we use for technical SEO audits. It’s helpful to regularly audit large websites and ensure technical issues get identified and fixed quickly.
- [Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/) is a comprehensive SEO toolset that can help manage large-scale link-building campaigns.
- [SEMRush](https://www.semrush.com/) is another all-in-one SEO tool that allows for in-depth market research. Its ability to track and compare large volumes of data allows for this.
- [Looker Studio](https://lookerstudio.google.com/u/0/navigation/reporting) lets us create custom reports and dashboards, compiling data from multiple sources. Previously known as Google Data Studio, Looker Studio allows for the visualisation of complex data in accessible ways, making it easier to communicate insights to your stakeholders and make data-driven decisions.

These tools are foundational for any successful enterprise SEO strategy.

## How to Setup Analytics for Enterprise SEO

We know that a sophisticated analytics framework to track performance and extract actionable insights is needed by enterprise companies. Some of the steps that need to be taken to ensure analytics are properly set up include:

### Advanced Goal Tracking

At the enterprise level, we understand that there needs to be alignment with the largest business goals. We go well beyond tracking conversions. Instead, we’re looking at understanding the customer journey across multiple touchpoints.

We track micro-conversions like video plays or specific user interactions, which indicate deeper engagement. We use Google Tag Manager to implement event tracking and create custom goals to reflect particular business KPIs.

### Multi-domain and Subdomain Tracking

Enterprises often manage multiple domains and subdomains, each with its own purpose or geographic region that it serves. Cross-domain tracking is necessary to understand user behaviour across all web properties.

We configure analytics tools to recognise user sessions spanning multiple domains. The goal is to provide a unified view of the customer’s journey without data fragmentation.

### Custom Dashboards and Reporting

The volume of data at the enterprise level makes custom dashboards a must. Tools like Looker Studio or Tableau can create tailored dashboards that pull from multiple sources, including Google Analytics, Search Console, and CRM systems.

### Implementing Advanced Segmentation

Advanced segmentation lets you dig into your data and uncover insights otherwise not apparent when viewing aggregate data. Enterprise SEO reporting techniques involve creating segments based on metrics like customer lifetime value or traffic sources.

### A/B Testing and Experimentation

The key to optimising SEO efforts, especially at scale, is testing. We implement [A/B testing](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/website-testing) to determine the site changes that lead to the best outcomes. It can be as simple as testing headlines or as complex as changing site structure.

Using tools like Google Optimize helps run these experiences and ensures your analytics setup accurately tracks the tests’ impact on SEO metrics.

### Ensuring Data Accuracy

Enterprise SEO is highly complex, making data integrity a main priorities. We regularly audit your analytics setup to ensure tracking codes are working correctly and there are no data discrepancies. We encourage setting up alerts for unusual data patterns so they can be addressed before they escalate.

### Attribution Modeling

At the enterprise level, understanding the full impact of SEO efforts requires sophisticated attribution modelling. You want to move beyond last-click attribution models. Instead, look for models that credit all the touchpoints along the customer’s journey.

## What Reports Should You Build?

As enterprise SEO professionals, we know that the scale of operations and the complexity of your data require reporting that goes beyond standard metrics.

Your reports should provide insights into your SEO performance, align with business objectives, uncover opportunities and address specific challenges. The key reports that need to be built to drive actionable insights at the enterprise level include:

### Executive Summary Reports

The goal is to align SEO performance with objectives for the business and key stakeholder interests.

Executive summary reports help you communicate the impact of SEO efforts to C-suite executives and other non-technical stakeholders. These reports should focus on high-level metrics and show the connection between SEO initiatives and revenue growth or cost savings.

These reports need to emphasise how SEO is contributing to broader business strategy.

### Keyword Performance Reports

The goal of these reports in enterprise SEO analytics is to monitor your keyword strategy across multiple markets or regions. You want to track keywords at a granular level to understand localised performance.

Actionable insights from these reports include high-performing keywords to focus on and underperforming ones that you may need to refine or replace.

### Content Performance Reports

Evaluate your content’s impact on SEO performance and user engagement.

Massive amounts of content may be managed across multiple sites at the enterprise level. Content performance reports can examine metrics like page views, time on page and conversions that can be attributed to particular pieces of content.

Identify top-performing content and replicate its success; on the flip side, find underperforming content that needs to be updated or optimised.

### Technical SEO Audit Reports

Technical SEO audit reports monitor a website’s health. Technical issues can severely impact SEO performance, especially in an enterprise with large, complex sites.

Generating detailed technical SEO audit reports regularly can help identify and fix crawl errors, site speed issues, and problems with mobile usability.

Technical fixes should be prioritised based on their potential impact on SEO goals, such as resolving issues affecting many high-priority pages.

### Local SEO Performance Reports

If you’re an enterprise with multiple locations, track performance across multiple locations or regions. Local SEO performance reports can track metrics, including Google My Business (GMB) insights, local keyword rankings, and location-specific page traffic.

Identify regions where your local SEO efforts aren’t performing well and adjust strategies.

### Competitor Analysis Reports

Understand the SEO strategies of competitors by building reports to see how they’re performing in search, the keywords they’re ranking for and where they might have an advantage.

Reports should include keyword ranking comparisons, backlink profiles, domain authority and content strategies.

### Custom Conversion Tracking Reports

Custom conversion tracking reports can tie SEO efforts directly to lead generation and revenue. The reports can track user actions such as form submissions or purchases. Segment data by traffic source or user behaviour for deeper insights.

Then, you can use these reports to understand the SEO actions leading to the highest conversion rates and inform your site structure, technical optimisation, and content strategy.

## Advanced Reporting Techniques

There is plenty of data in enterprise SEO analytics. The challenge lies in making it understandable and actionable. Advanced reporting techniques, especially visualisation and dashboards, take raw data and turn it into meaningful insights to drive decision-making at every level.

Tools like Looker Studio, previously known as Google Data Studio, allow users to create impactful reports.

Custom dashboards in these tools allow you to create a visual, real-time representation of your most critical SEO metrics. Through connections with multiple data sources, you can display KPIs. You get an at-a-glance view of your SEO health.

Examples of visualisations and dashboards include:

- **Interactive heat maps** with tools like Crazy Egg integrated into your reporting system can help you see user behaviour on your site. You can visualise the areas of your pages receiving the most attention. Use the data to decide page layout, content distribution, and CTA placement.
- **Funnel visualisations** track the user journey from the initial site visit to conversion. In an enterprise context, these can involve multiple touchpoints and channels. Looker Studio can be used to build funnel visualisations that track drop-offs at every stage.
- For enterprises operating across regions or countries, **geographic performance maps** help visualise where SEO efforts are doing well. With Looker Studio, you can overlay data on a map to represent your geographic SEO performance.
- **Competitor comparison reports** can be created with data from tools like Ahrefs or SEMRush. You can compare domain authority, backlink profiles, keyword rankings and traffic levels. Bar or radar charts are good ways to compare metrics against competitors.

With advanced reporting techniques, you can transform complex SEO data into something clear and accessible. It’s also worth noting that generative AI in SEO is especially relevant in analytics and reporting.

Generative AI makes it possible to process and analyse large volumes of SEO data faster and more accurately than traditional methods. It can automate SEO reports and enhance reporting with predictive analysis, improving data visualisation with dynamic, engaging representations.

## What Should Enterprise Companies Be Tracking?

Every enterprise-level organisation will have metrics that are the most valuable to track. In our opinion, based on our experience and overall enterprise SEO trends, some of the metrics we find are valuable to track include:

- **Organic market share** measures the percentage of search traffic captured relative to competitors in the same industry.
- **Cross-domain traffic** helps understand how users navigate different parts of the enterprise digital ecosystem. It can help assess internal linking strategies and user flows across web properties.
- **Global and regional keyword rankings** include monitoring how the company performs in different locations and languages. Regional keyword rankings help enterprises tailor their SEO strategies to local markets.
- **Enterprise-level backlink profiles** . Managing a large backlink profile includes acquiring high-quality links and regularly auditing to disavow spammy or harmful links that could affect the ranking of the entire domain.
- **Core Web Vitals across multiple sites** . Enterprises often have multiple websites or sites with thousands of pages. Tracking Core Web Vitals across these sites is needed to ensure all the properties meet Google performance standards and maintain overall site health.
- **Content efficiency metrics** include the return on content investment and the performance of content clusters. Enterprises producing large volumes of content need to track how well specific pieces of content perform in driving traffic, engagement and conversions relative to the resources spent to create them.
- **Enterprise-level technical SEO metrics** . These can include crawl budget optimisation, site architecture and page load speeds across large and complex sites. Search engines should be able to crawl and index all pages efficiently.
- **Internal search metrics** like click-through rates and search query data can be important. These provide insight into what users are looking for on teh site. This allows enterprises to optimise navigation, improve user experience, and ensure that high-demand content is easily accessible.
- **Brand and non-brand traffic** need to be segmented to understand the full impact of SEO efforts. Brand traffic reflects existing customer loyalty, while non-brand traffic indicates outreach and acquisition scenes. Tracking them separately helps balance brand reinforcement with growth in new audience segments.

Finally, we also think metrics can be valuable, including **revenue by channel.** There needs to be granularity that lets enterprises understand the SEO strategies or content pieces directly contributing to revenue and how their organic search efforts complement other marketing channels. 

## FAQs

### What metrics should be included in an enterprise SEO report?

An enterprise SEO report can include metrics like organic traffic, keyword rankings, bounce rates, backlink profile data, and conversion rates from organic searches. Technical issues like Core Web Vitals and mobile usability are also necessary for enterprise SEO analytics.

### How often should SEO reports be generated for an enterprise?

Our general recommendation is that reports are generated monthly for enterprise SEO. This gives a comprehensive overview of performance trends, but more frequent reporting, like weekly dashboards, can also be useful. Frequent reporting lets us track key real-time metrics to quickly address issues.

### What is the role of dashboards in SEO reporting?

Dashboards give us a visual representation of key SEO metrics in real-time, allowing us to monitor performance at a glance. They’re especially important in enterprise SEO analytics because they consolidate data from various sources, making it easier to spot trends and issues and make informed decisions.

### How do you ensure the accuracy of SEO analytics data?

To ensure accuracy, we encourage regular auditing of tracking set up with tools like Google Tag Manager for event tracking. Tools like Google Tag Assistant can be used to validate data. It’s also important to cross-track data from multiple analytics platforms.

### What should be included in an SEO conversion tracking report?

An SEO conversion tracking report should include the number of conversions from organic traffic, conversion rates, and conversions’ value. It should also include the user journey that led to those conversions. You can then segment the data by keyword, landing page and traffic source for deeper insights into what’s driving your conversions.

When we focus on the right metrics, use sophisticated analytics techniques and regularly generate actionable reports, we help enterprise organisations track their SEO performance while making data-guided decisions to drive significant business growth.

## Enterprise SEO Best Practices

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/16-enterprise-seo-best-practices-your-company-should-have/

# 16 Enterprise SEO Best Practices Your Company Should Have

Enterprise SEO companies have to do SEO at scale to optimise hundreds or even thousands of pages. Plus, you’re competing against sites with large budgets and established teams.

Understanding enterprise SEO best practices will give your website the best possible foundation to grow. With our decade of [enterprise SEO agency](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/) experience managing enterprise clients, we know what a good foundation looks like. 

## Comprehensive Keyword Research and Targeting

Knowing how to find keywords and what ones to target are two of the most important aspects of search engine optimisation. Without this, you’re going to struggle to drive meaningful traffic to your website.


It’s considered best practice to divide keywords into different groups:


- Informational
- Commercial
- Transactional


This will give you a clear strategy to map keywords to revenue increase. Most sites will want to create topical maps that aim to boost the ranking of transactional pages with supporting informational content

## On-Page Optimisation (Titles, Meta Descriptions, Headers)

Titles should include primary keywords and be short (less than 60 characters) to avoid shortening their appearance in search results. Also, your title should be compelling to a reader, utilising intrigue to improve your CTR.


Meta descriptions provide a content summary and offer a call to action (CTA), encouraging viewers to buy a product or service. These descriptions should be unique for each webpage, which can be time-consuming.


Lastly, headers (H1, H2, and H3) should naturally integrate keywords and their variations. All of the information on the site should fit together for an enterprise brand.

## Technical SEO Audits and Fixes

Website crawlers can help identify crawl issues, such as broken links, 301 chains, and pages with no index tags. Spend time inspecting the URL structure, making sure that the URLs are clean and descriptive enough for the site.


Another important aspect of technical SEO is optimising site speed. Users will not want to stay on a site that is slow, so compressing images and leveraging caching are two ways to accomplish this.

## High-Quality, Relevant Content Creation

The quality and relevancy of your content will improve your search rankings, as Google prioritises content that will serve searchers in the most efficient and impactful way.


Make sure the content you post is highly relevant to the search query. Also, take older content and revamp it every few months to ensure search engines see it as fresh and you’re not providing out-of-date information.

## Mobile Optimisation

Over 50% of searches are done on mobile and Google now indexes everything mobile-first. If your site doesn’t perform well on mobile you’ll lose rankings and customers.


You may have to rework the site design to be suitable for mobile. This includes UI fixes as well as technical SEO fixes. Having a technical SEO expert work with your designer is necessary to have both departments working well.

## Structured Data and Schema Markup Implementation

As SEO professionals, search engines must understand and categorise the content on your enterprise site appropriately. Structured data provides a blueprint for information, classifying the content on that page into categories like products, bios, reviews, and more.


Implementing structured data will allow your content to receive rich results which can be helpful for CTR and to push your competitors further down in the SERPs.

## Backlink Building and Outreach

Backlink building involves thorough research of competitors and their backlink strategies, which can be done with tools like SEMrush and Ahrefs. Performing a link intersect can allow your website to capture the links that your competitors have.


A good outreach strategy also helps to build connections as well as boost your organic rankings. Build links to your transactional pages. Ranking these pages higher is the best way to increase revenue with SEO.

## Local SEO Strategies

If your enterprise business targets specific regions, you want a strategy to reflect that. Geo-targeted landing pages will help you capture location-specific keywords. These keywords tend to convert better as they better suit searchers intent.

## Regular SEO Performance Monitoring and Reporting

Take time to plan quarterly and annual SEO goals. These could be increasing registration through SEO or increasing overall traffic by X%. Whatever it is, having a way to track and report goals improves the chances of achieving them.


Enterprise sites usually have multiple strategies going at once, so using a dashboard system can be really helpful for seeing all of the data in one place.

## Internal Linking Strategy

Websites can use internal linking to rank higher in search engines. This is because enterprise SEO benefits from strategically linking to high-authority pages to improve site navigation.


This approach doesn’t just help search engines – it also improves user experience, as it guides visitors to various pages on a site. This encourages them to stay for longer than they would have without the links.

## SEO-Friendly URL Structures

Every SEO professional should create URLs to be clear, short, and descriptive. Care should also be taken to avoid 301 redirect loops when URLs need to be changed. Track URL statuses in a spreadsheet to ensure that URLs are healthy.

## Consistent Content Updates and Refreshes

Content updates and refreshes keep an enterprise site relevant. Rewriting blog posts and updating product pages all tie into a successful SEO strategy. Ultimately, if a user does not feel that a site matches what they are looking for, they will search for one that does. This signals to Google that your page isn’t useful which can lower its ranking.

## Competitor Analysis and Benchmarking

Competitor analysis and benchmarking is how you beat your competitors. Performing a SWOT analysis is a good place to start.


- Strengths
- Weaknesses
- Opportunities
- Threats


This will show you what you need to be doing. Maybe there’s a content gap you’re missing or perhaps their backlink profile is stronger. This information is invaluable when looking to climb rankings and improve your SEO ROI. If you see that your site is falling behind, you may need to rework your SEO strategy to make it more effective and results-oriented.

## Implementation of SEO Best Practices for E-commerce (if applicable)

If your SEO team works on enterprise [e-commerce sites](https://www.sana-commerce.com/e-commerce-terms/what-is-e-commerce-seo/), the implementation of SEO matters. All of the above content is particularly relevant, but you will also want to include a site structure with clear categories and fast page loading times. With this, you’ll rank up toward the top of the search engine list in no time. 

## Compliance with Search Engine Guidelines

Search engine guidelines are essential to follow for SEO professionals and enterprise sites. Check out Google’s Webmaster Guidelines ([Google Search Essentials](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials)) for specific information. Black hat SEO or even misinformed mistakes are even more costly for enterprise businesses. 

## Regular Training for the SEO Team

A good practice to get into is regularly encourage collaboration and training within your team. What works for SEO today may not work next week or next month. Staying up-to-date on the latest algorithm updates and practices will only advance your business in the long run.

Setting up all of the enterprise SEO best practices in-house just isn’t time or cost-effective for many companies. The Prosperity Media team has performed successful SEO strategies for many businesses just like yours. ## Four Pillars of Enterprise SEO

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/4-pillars-of-enterprise-seo/

# 4 Pillars of Enterprise SEO

The key to success in enterprise SEO is having a coordinated strategy and providing a purpose to everything you do. These purposes can be classified as the four pillars of enterprise SEO, and every action you take to optimize your website should elevate one of these four pillars.


In this post, we will explore these four pillars and provide actionable steps proven to yield results throughout our decade of providing [enterprise SEO services](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/) for companies in Australia, the US, and Europe.


## What are the 4 Pillars of Enterprise SEO?

Enterprise level SEO involves several complex processes that work cohesively to improve your brand’s online visibility. However, while there are dozens of individual steps, every action can be classified under one of the four pillars of enterprise SEO.


- **Mitigation** – Frequent technical audits and security measures ensure your website’s overall health and stability, catching technical SEO issues before they happen.
- **Analytics and Reporting** – Constant monitoring and analytics encourage data-driven adjustments to your strategy for better overall performance.
- **Growth Plan** – Effective content and link-building strategies help expand your search engine rankings and generate more organic traffic to your enterprise website.
- **Relationship & Company Approva** l – Open communication helps build internal relationships and generates support for current and future SEO initiatives.


In our experience, an enterprise SEO campaign that embraces these four pillars not only generates better results but yields a better execution of the strategy itself.


Along with promoting your brand with data-driven decisions, keyword research, and content production, the pillars also ensure a cohesive work experience among your enterprise SEO team and stronger internal support for your enterprise business’ search engine optimization efforts.


## Mitigation: Ensuring Site Health and Stability

One of the most important pillars of enterprise SEO is mitigation and error management. When dealing with enterprise websites for large companies, any website downtime can yield massive revenue losses.


As such, one of the key aspects of a successful enterprise SEO campaign is catching any technical issues before they become a problem. To do this, you need to have open communication between your technical SEO and engineering teams.


While all errors and bugs are ideally fleshed out before launch, a successful mitigation strategy also involves conducting regular technical audits to ensure everything continues to run smoothly.


This includes uncovering and correcting common issues such as broken links, duplicate content, slow page speeds, and mobile usability problems, enacting security measures to safeguard enterprise sites from external threats, and staying up to date with [Google Webmaster Guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials) and other search engine algorithms to avoid penalties.


## Analytics and Reporting: Data-Driven Decision Making

Enterprise SEO teams need to be able to prove results benefiting key performance metrics like search traffic and revenue. Otherwise, it may appear that your SEO efforts are just a drain on company funds. This is why proper analytics and reporting are a foundational pillar of enterprise SEO.


Unfortunately, Google doesn’t provide straightforward insights for its search engine traffic. Instead, SEO experts are required to collect data from search engines through various sources, including [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about), [Google Analytics](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/), and other search engines’ reporting tools.


While paid SEO tools, such as [SEMrush](https://www.semrush.com/) and [Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/), can make collecting this data a little easier, it still requires an SEO analytics expert to stitch all of the data points together to curate an understanding of where a website’s organic search volume is coming from and how it translates into revenue.


With over a decade of experience working with enterprise clients, we know exactly how your data comes together and can generate SEO insights to current SEO is performing, which of your current efforts are generating the best results, and identify opportunity areas for improvement.


## Growth Plan: Scalable Tactics for Enhanced Online Presence

One of the key metrics used to evaluate the success of any SEO campaign is organic traffic and how effective the campaign is in driving consistent, sustainable traffic to your website.


As such, having a detailed growth plan is a pivotal pillar for the long-term success of an enterprise SEO strategy and is the responsibility of the project manager.


Using the opportunities identified by the analytics team, it is the project manager’s role to execute a strategy that targets those holes.


This could be overhauling the design or content quality on specific pages, enacting an internal linking strategy, executing content creation using relevant target keywords to reach your target audience, or growing your domain authority through backlink outreach.


With this pillar being all about the project management of the SEO campaign, it is essential for the project manager to maintain consistent communication between various marketing teams to ensure a cohesive workflow and environment amongst all involved individuals and relevant stakeholders.

## Relationship Building and Company Approval: Securing Internal Support

The final pillar of enterprise SEO is securing internal support by building relationships and gaining company approval. This pillar requires an expert with strong communication skills to effectively detail the strategy and targets of your SEO campaign, ensuring your efforts are aligned with the overall business goals of your company.


By fostering these strong internal relationships and securing the approval of key stakeholders, you are creating an environment where SEO initiatives can thrive, opening the door to success and the possibility of future initiatives.


The key to nurturing these relationships is through open communication between stakeholders and cross-department collaboration. A good enterprise SEO team works closely with several departments, including IT, engineering, sales, creative, legal, and public relations.


It is essential to maintain relationships within each of these departments to ensure an effective collaboration when you ultimately need to work alongside one or more of these teams.


## How Can I Implement the Pillars of Enterprise SEO in My Business?

Implementing the pillars of enterprise SEO is a great way to focus your overall SEO efforts on a strategy that yields results.


However, doing it right requires a careful and methodical approach to ensure each aspect is properly integrated into your business operations while maintaining a cohesive strategy, goals, and mission.


Here are a few tips on how you can begin effectively integrating the elements of these pillars into your current enterprise SEO strategy.


- **Develop a Comprehensive Road Map** – Ensure a cohesive vision across all pillars by creating a visual strategy that incorporates elements of all four pillars while maintaining a uniform purpose.
- **Allocate Resources** – Establish the resources, budget, and personnel required to support each pillar. Using advanced SEO tools can help you determine which pillars to prioritize.
- **Encourage Collaboration** – Reach out to key stakeholders across departments to generate personal investment within your SEO strategy and gain support for current and future initiatives.
- **Monitor and Adjust** – Use analytics tools to continuously track performance and adapt your SEO strategies using data-driven adjustments.


## Want to Bolster Your Enterprise SEO?


While this is a great way to start introducing the elements of the pillars of enterprise SEO into your current digital marketing strategy, you don’t have to do it alone.


Tap into a decade of enterprise SEO experience with Prosperity Media’s dedicated SEO and marketing team and engage sophisticated strategies proven to integrate mitigation, analytics and reporting, growth plan, and relationships and company approval into your SEO strategy.

## Essential Enterprise SEO Tips

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/8-enterprise-seo-tips-every-enterprise-should-know/

# 8 Enterprise SEO Tips Every Enterprise Should Know

From managing large-scale websites to competing with massive corporations with multi-million dollar marketing budgets, enterprise SEO is one of the most difficult and complex fields to operate in and requires an experienced enterprise SEO team.

Luckily, you can streamline your digital marketing strategy by following these enterprise SEO tips featuring scalable tactics and insights developed over our ten years of experience working as an [enterprise SEO agency](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/).

## Expand Content Internationally

One of the biggest challenges when handling enterprise-level SEO is expanding your business’s online visibility to international audiences. However, instead of spending countless hours researching, creating, and distributing fresh content, the easiest way to expand your reach on scale is by repurposing your existing pages.


The key to doing this successfully is first identifying your top-performing content and the areas you would like to expand into. From there, you simply need to translate and localise those top-performing pages and posts, ensuring they are accessible to different markets.


Do this successfully, and watch as you tap into new global audiences and drive more organic traffic to your enterprise business website.

## Regularly Refresh Content

Enterprise SEO differs from traditional SEO in that everything needs to be done on scale. This includes content creation.


The problem is that when taking into account ideation, research, writing, and editing, creating and publishing even a single piece of content can take a lot of time and resources. Fortunately, you can supplement your content publication schedule simply by updating your existing pieces of content.


Not only does updating a page or blog post require less time than creating a new piece of content from scratch, but it also ensures that the piece of content remains relevant with fresh and updated information, keeping it as an authoritative resource for its target query and in a prevalent position on search engine result pages.

## Implement Schema Markup

While not a direct ranking factor, schema markup can be a powerful technical SEO tool for driving traffic to your website and establishing your enterprise company as an authority in your market.


There are many different [types of schema markups](https://schema.org/docs/schemas.html), but each one provides structural data that offers contextual information for search engines as to what your page is about. Additionally, search engines, such as Google, use these markups to determine eligibility for rich snippets.


By using schema markup like product markup, review markup, and local business markup, enterprise companies can show search engines what content on their website to prioritise, potentially boosting your online visibility to relevant audiences.

## Perform Content Gap Analysis

By nature of working with large corporations, enterprise SEO is an extremely competitive field. As such, a great way to ensure you maintain your competitive edge over your competition is by performing frequent content gap analysis as part of your enterprise SEO strategy.

Through a content gap analysis, you can determine keywords that your competitors are ranking for that you aren’t. From there, you can begin planning an effective content strategy to outrank your competitors for those keywords, siphoning organic leads from their enterprise website to yours.

Here is a brief overview to how you can perform a proper content gap analysis and get a leg up over your competition:


1. Identify your top SEO competitors.
2. Use tools like [Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/) or[SEMrush](https://www.semrush.com/) to determine your competitors’ top-performing content.
3. Evaluate your existing content for gaps and conduct keyword research.
4. Begin planning content to fill gaps using competitive keywords.


## Optimise Internal Linking

Internal link building is one of those search engine optimisation practices that often gets swept under the rug when working with enterprise sites.

But in our experience, internal links pose a great opportunity to influence user engagement and boost conversions while helping search engines understand the structure of your website in the process.

Here are a few tips for optimising the internal link structure of your enterprise site.


- **Use Descriptive Anchor Texts** – Search engines use anchor texts to provide context to the target page. You should leverage this strategically.
- **Link to High-Value Pages** – Prioritise linking to key web pages that either drive conversions or further nurture your leads.
- **Balance Your Link Distribution** – Ensure you use internal links evenly throughout your website, avoiding instances of overloading any single page.


The problem that arises when doing internal link building for enterprise SEO is that you are often working with websites with thousands or millions of pages. In these instances, a great technique is to separate your pages into related groups, inserting internal links where relevant.

## Leverage Digital PR

When it comes to enterprise SEO, you need to generate backlinks on a scale. This is where a [digital PR services](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/digital-pr-agency/) come in. 


Unlike other link building tactics that focus on a single link at a time, such as guest posting and broken link outreach, digital PR targets an umbrella of websites to earn high-quality and authoritative backlinks that direct back to your enterprise website.


We do this through three techniques:


- **Reactive Digital PR** – Add authority to current news stories with expert commentary and quotes.
- **Proactive Digital PR** – Provide linkable assets by repurposing existing content, such as blog posts, whitepapers, and first-party data.
- **Campaign-led Digital PR** – Create original and compelling content specifically for digital PR efforts.


When done correctly, an effective digital PR campaign not only drives traffic back to your website but also boosts your brand awareness and credibility, quickly elevating you as a trusted authority.

## Utilise AI and Automation

While AI software isn’t a do-it-all solution, it is undoubtedly a fantastic resource for automating some of the monotonous aspects of enterprise SEO and should be leveraged for introducing certain elements at scale.


In fact, up to [64% of business owners](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/business/ai-statistics/) believe and rely on AI to improve business productivity, and the AI market is expected to grow to [$407 billion by 2027](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/business/ai-statistics/). As such, learning how to incorporate AI into your daily tasks should be at the forefront of your enterprise SEO strategy.


While AI isn’t quite up to the task of taking over your more creative marketing and SEO efforts, a few areas it can help automate include:


- Brainstorming content ideas
- Generating content briefs and outlines
- Facilitating research processes
- Optimising pages for SEO
- 
## Engage Advanced Tracking and Reporting Techniques

Being able to effectively track and report your SEO performance is a pillar of an enterprise SEO strategy. Depending on who you are reporting to, these results can range from simple business KPIs (key performance indicators) to detailed breakdowns of various SEO metrics.


An enterprise SEO analyst knows how to track and report on key metrics, such as organic traffic, search engine rankings, and conversion rates.


While advanced tools like [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console/about), Ahrefs, and SEMrush can aid in the collection of these data points, it takes an experienced professional to understand how they come together to establish organic revenue and ROI insights.

## Enterprise SEO Technology Insights

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo-technology/

# Enterprise SEO Technology

Enterprise companies face unique challenges regarding search engine optimisation. The complexity of large websites, the need for advanced tools, and the pressure to maintain a strong online presence demand a detailed and tailored enterprise SEO strategy.

With over a decade of experience in [enterprise SEO services](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/), we’ve seen firsthand how leveraging the right technology can significantly impact achieving and maintaining top rankings in search engines. Our enterprise SEO focuses on delivering effective SEO, ensuring these strategies provide measurable results. We’ll share the technology we use so you can do the same to improve your SEO. 

## **Enterprise SEO Platforms and Technology That We Use**

When working with enterprise clients, the tools and technologies we use are critical to our success. Enterprise SEO platforms are designed to handle the scale and complexity of large websites, providing the insights and capabilities needed to optimise effectively.

In our experience, the right SEO tools can mean the difference between a strategy that merely maintains rankings and one that dominates the SERPs, which is why we incorporate top-tier SEO services in our approach.

## **Keyword Research and Analysis Tools**

Keyword research is the foundation of any SEO strategy. For enterprise-level SEO, the stakes are higher, and the competition is tougher. That’s why we rely on advanced SEO tools that go beyond basic search volume and competition metrics.

1. [**SEMrush**](https://www.semrush.com/) : SEMrush is a powerful tool that provides comprehensive keyword analysis, competitor insights, and market trends. For enterprise SEO, SEMrush allows us to identify high-impact keywords that align with our client’s business goals. When working with our enterprise clients, we’ve seen SEMrush reveal opportunities that were previously hidden.
2. [**Ahrefs**](https://ahrefs.com/) : Known for its extensive backlink database, Ahrefs is also a go-to tool for SEO competitive analysis. It helps us uncover opportunities by analysing competitors’ rankings and identifying gaps in our clients’ content. We’ve seen good results with Ahrefs, especially when used to pinpoint and target high-value SEO strategies that our client’s competitors were excelling in, but they weren’t.
3. [**Google Keyword Planner**](https://ads.google.com/) : While it’s a standard tool, Google Keyword Planner is still invaluable for enterprise SEO. It provides accurate data straight from the source—Google itself—helping us make data-driven decisions about which keywords to target.

## **On-Page Optimisation Tools**

On-page SEO is crucial for ensuring that each website page is optimised for search engines and users alike. For enterprise sites, enterprise SEO solutions are essential to manage the complexities of hundreds or even thousands of pages.

1. [**Surfer SEO**](https://surferseo.com/) : Surfer SEO takes on-page optimisation to the next level by analysing the top-ranking pages for a given keyword and providing data-driven recommendations. This helps us fine-tune content to meet the specific requirements of Google’s algorithm. When working with our clients, Surfer SEO has enabled us to optimise content that ranks consistently in the top 3 positions for highly competitive keywords.

These tools are essential for managing the complexities of on-page SEO at the enterprise level, ensuring that every page on the site is optimised to its full potential in line with SEO best practices.

## **Technical SEO Tools**

Technical SEO is the backbone of any successful enterprise SEO strategy. It involves optimising the infrastructure of a website to ensure that search engines can easily crawl and index its pages, which is important for implementing a comprehensive enterprise SEO strategy that delivers long-term results.

Enterprise SEO refers to handling the complexities of optimising websites, ensuring that every technical aspect is addressed to enhance search engine visibility. By addressing various aspects of technical SEO, businesses can ensure that their websites are both search engine-friendly and user-friendly, setting the stage for effective optimisation.

1. [**Google Search Console**](https://search.google.com/search-console/about) : Google Search Console is a must-have tool for monitoring and maintaining a website’s presence in Google search results. It provides insights into how Google views a site and helps us identify and fix technical issues. In our experience, regular monitoring has prevented potential problems before they could impact our clients’ enterprise SEO rankings.
2. [**DeepCrawl**](https://www.lumar.io/) : DeepCrawl is an enterprise-grade tool that provides in-depth technical audits of websites. It helps us identify crawl errors, site speed problems, and security vulnerabilities.
3. [**Botify**](https://www.botify.com/) : Botify is another powerful tool that focuses on technical SEO. It provides detailed insights into how search engines interact with a website, allowing us to optimise crawl efficiency and improve overall site performance.
4. [**Screaming Frog SEO Spider**](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk/seo-spider/) : This tool is invaluable for crawling large websites, and identifying on-page issues such as broken links, duplicate content, and missing metadata. It allows us to audit and optimise large-scale sites quickly.

By using these enterprise SEO tools as part of your comprehensive enterprise SEO, you can ensure that your websites are not only visible to search engines but also perform well in terms of speed, security, and overall user experience.

Conducting a thorough enterprise SEO audit helps us identify opportunities for further optimisation, ensuring our strategies are always data-driven and effective. A positive user experience is crucial for keeping visitors engaged and reducing bounce rates, contributing to higher search rankings.

## **Backlink Analysis Tools**

Backlinks remain an important factor in SEO, especially for enterprise sites, and an enterprise SEO agency that needs to establish authority and trustworthiness in their industry. Partnering with an enterprise SEO agency can provide tailored strategies and data-driven approaches to manage these complex needs effectively.

1. **Majestic SEO** : Majestic is one of the most comprehensive backlink analysis tools available. It provides detailed information about the quality and quantity of backlinks, helping us assess the strength of our clients’ link profiles. As an enterprise SEO agency, leveraging Majestic has been key to delivering measurable improvements in our clients’ backlink profiles.
2. **Ahrefs** : Ahrefs excels in backlink analysis, offering a vast database of links and robust reporting features. It allows us to track new links, analyse competitors’ link profiles, and identify link-building opportunities. When working with our enterprise clients, Ahrefs has been useful in recovering lost backlinks and securing new ones that significantly improved our clients’ search rankings. This tool is a staple in our enterprise SEO agency toolkit for achieving top-tier link-building results.

These tools are important in building and maintaining a strong backlink profile, essential for improving search engine rankings and driving organic traffic in enterprise SEO.

## **SEO Analytics and Reporting Software**

For enterprise clients, analytics and reporting tools that can handle large datasets and provide actionable insights are necessary.

1. **Google Analytics** : Google Analytics is the gold standard for web analytics. It provides detailed insights into user behaviour, traffic sources, and conversion rates, helping us measure the effectiveness of our enterprise SEO strategies.
2. **Google Looker Studio** : Google’s Data Studio is a powerful tool for creating custom reports and dashboards. It allows us to visualise data from multiple sources, making it easier for our clients to understand the impact of our enterprise SEO efforts. In our experience, Looker Studio has been invaluable in providing clear, actionable insights that help our clients make data-driven decisions that enhance their enterprise SEO performance.

These tools are essential for tracking the performance of our enterprise SEO refers, identifying areas for improvement, and demonstrating ROI to our clients, all integral aspects of an enterprise SEO technology stack.

## **What Are the Key Features to Look For?**

When selecting tools and platforms for enterprise SEO, it’s important to consider the specific needs of your business and the role of search engine optimisation. In our experience, the following features are critical:

- **Scalability** : The ability to handle large amounts of data and scale with your business is crucial for enterprise SEO.
- **Customisation** : The ability to customise tools and reports to meet the unique needs of your business.
- **Integration** : The ability to integrate with other tools and platforms, such as CRM and marketing automation tools.
- **Support** : Access to dedicated support and resources to help you get the most out of your enterprise SEO tools.

We’ve seen good results when our clients choose tools that offer these features, ensuring their technology can grow and evolve with their business needs.

## **What Are The Benefits of Technology for Enterprise SEO?**

Leveraging the right technology can provide numerous benefits, including:

- **Improved Efficiency** : Automation and advanced tools can help streamline many aspects of enterprise SEO, from content optimisation to reporting.
- **Better Decision-Making** : Access to accurate, real-time data allows for more informed decisions and more effective enterprise SEO strategies.
- **Increased ROI** : By optimising your enterprise SEO, you can achieve better results with less effort, leading to a higher return on investment.

## **Importance of Enterprise SEO for Businesses**

Specific enterprise SEO is needed to perform well in highly competitive markets. There are several key benefits when it comes to SEO for enterprises.

- **Increase Visibility** : By optimising relevant keywords and improving site performance, enterprise SEO and local SEO help businesses rank higher in search engine results.
- **Drive Traffic** : Higher rankings lead to increased organic traffic, which can drive more leads and sales.
- **Build Authority** : A strong online presence helps establish your business as a leader in your industry, building trust and credibility with your audience.

## Top Enterprise SEO Reporting Tools

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/best-enterprise-seo-reporting-software/

# Best Enterprise SEO Reporting Software

Optimising your online marketing efforts is the goal of all enterprise businesses and a wealth of different products are out there to help you do just that. Investing in the right software is crucial for the best SEO and competitive analysis, so your content creation and search engine optimisation are always on point.

Our [enterprise SEO agency](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/enterprise-seo/) experience means we know what gets results. Here is a quick view of some of the top enterprise SEO reporting software, plus guidance on the key features to look out for when investing in reporting and enterprise SEO software. 

## **Best Enterprise SEO Reporting Software**

Reporting software is vital in monitoring search engine results, search engine rankings and competitor analysis as part of a SEO strategy and successful content optimisation. Some reporting software focuses on specific features, with other products which offer a whole suite of options.

The right choice comes down to the size of your business, whether you have multiple websites and the key tasks you want to perform. Here are four of the best enterprise SEO tools we recommend when working with our enterprise clients.

### **Keyword Tracking: Advanced Web Tracking**

Advanced web tracking provides metrics to evaluate your website’s performance on search engines. Picking the right tracking metrics for your business is important. The most commonly used are keyword rankings and organic traffic conversions.

Advanced web tjelps your keyword research, tracking your keyword performance on a range of sites not just Google, and taking a deep dive into user behavior and performance.

As part of your enterprise SEO tools, keyword tracking helps promote superior content creation and increases your website’s online visibility with better search engine rankings. Prove that your keyword research is delivering keyword performance.

### **Data Visualisation: Google Looker Studio**

For digital marketers, Google Looker is software that takes dry data and turns it into readable and easily comparable interactive visuals. If you need to visualise data, this is the right enterprise SEO tool for the job.

Google Looker Studio is Google analytics at its absolute best, a combo of Google Data Studio and Looker acquired by Google in 2020. It’s straightforward to use, so you don’t need a particular tech background to create informative dashboards using a drag-and-drop function.

### **Technical SEO: Screaming Frog**

Screaming Frog is an SEO Spider tool and the market leader for technical SEO audits, free to use although, if you want additional features, then you will need to purchase a license. Screaming Frog is the perfect tool for a site audit and picks up common SEO issues and, in our experience, it is one of the best enterprise SEO tools.

Screaming Frog provides up-to-date data with the option to schedule website crawls that report directly to your email. It will find duplicate pages, broken links and missing tags, working page by page and saving hours of time particularly if you have multiple websites. There is a deep crawling facility for e-commerce sites.

In our experience, clients find Screaming Frog easy to use for a site audit. It quickly becomes an essential amongst their SEO tools for search engine optimization and optimal search rankings.

### **Backlink Reporting: Ahrefs**

Ahrefs is probably best known as a backlink analysis and authority checker and is used by many digital marketers for link building strategies. However, Ahrefs has other valuable features like rank tracking and monitoring and is an effective keyword research tool. Users are provided with a complete suite of SEO tools with the object of helping websites focus their SEO efforts to improve their organic traffic and claim the top spots in Google search results.

Some key Ahrefs features include site audits to pick up broken links, backlink analysis, and traffic values on keywords with advanced features, including a keyword explorer for deep keyword research. Add to this rank tracking and content analysis, and you’ll see that Ahrefs is one of the most comprehensive SEO tools out there.

**Key Features to Look For**

### **Customisable Reports**

Customisable reporting is essential to fit your business’s specific needs and targets; ‘one size fits all’ just doesn’t cut it.

Flexible reporting will ensure that the SEO tools you use are always relevant, providing valuable insights which can inform your SEO strategy.

### **Comprehensive Data Integration**

Comprehensive data integration avoids the silo effect of looking at different data sets in isolation. Harmonising data from multiple sources provides advanced analytics, ironing out the challenges of blending data from a wide range of locations and making it ‘decision-ready’.

### **Regularly Updated**

Like any software, reporting software can have flaws and glitches. By updating regularly, you’ll protect your business against any security issues in weak areas. If you don’t update, you can be at risk. Equally, choosing software that offers regular updates is important – be wary if that’s not available.

Updates also bring performance enhancements, so you could miss out if you don’t bother staying current. Earlier versions of some reporting software may prove incompatible or troublesome with other SEO tools or systems, hampering your SEO efforts.

### **Integration Capabilities** 

The last thing any enterprise SEO business needs is reporting software that can’t integrate with other SEO tools and systems to streamline workflows and project management. This is another pain point that can cause data silos, just like a lack of comprehensive data integration.

Reporting software must integrate with your communication channels and the software you use to track and action issues in your businesses’ enterprise SEO strategy.

### **Scalability**

Scalability is essential in reporting software to manage increased workloads and add users without compromising the quality of reporting or increasing costs exponentially. This doesn’t just mean covering multiple websites but could be adding functions.

Scalability is about supporting growth whilst still being able to perform; this distinguishes the best reporting software from the ‘also rans’ and is a hallmark of some of the best enterprise SEO tools. But scalability also refers to contraction; this could be driven by seasonality in some businesses.

## **How Should Reporting Software Influence Your SEO?**

Reporting software is one of a suite of SEO tools that help you understand how your business performs on search engines. It is not an SEO strategy; instead, it informs and guides SEO strategies as one of a business’s essential SEO tools, confirms whether they are working, and, if not, provides data as to why not.

If your search volume is low, then reporting software can help you create optimised pages with deep keyword analysis and effective link building to lift a website’s search engine performance across multiple search engines.

Reporting software is the best SEO tool to improve online visibility but as with all things SEO, it is only part of a complex picture and should form part of a coherent suite of enterprise SEO software.

## Choosing an SEO Agency

Source: https://prosperitymedia.com.au/how-to-choose-an-seo-agency/

# How to Choose an SEO Agency

Experience and proven results are important when selecting the right SEO agency. With over a decade of expertise in SEO we’ve seen the good, the bad and everything inbetween.

SEO is more competitive and difficult than ever. Choosing the right [SEO company](https://prosperitymedia.com.au/seo-agency/) can be the difference between success and wasting your budget. This guide walks you through the key factors to remember when choosing an SEO agency.

## Understanding Your SEO Needs

Before you choose an SEO company, it’s crucial to clearly define your specific SEO needs and identify how they align with your broader business goals. Whether you want to expand your brand’s reach, improve local visibility or optimise a large-scale eCommerce site, understanding those needs will help you find an agency that can deliver the right strategy.

The following are key considerations you might set as goals in this phase of choosing an agency of SEO experts.

### Aligning SEO Strategy with Business Goals

In our experience, companies that focus on local SEO see significant growth by tailoring their strategies to regional markets. A targeted local SEO strategy can align with business goals to attract nearby customers.

### Technical SEO

If you aim to enhance your site’s technical SEO to improve the user experience and site performance, you’ll want to look for an agency with a strong technical background.

### Setting the Foundation for Success

Identifying your needs early helps you choose the right SEO agency and sets the foundation for a successful, goal-oriented SEO campaign. This alignment is key to ensuring your chosen SEO partner can deliver meaningful results to your business.

## Researching Potential Agencies

As you’re researching to find a good SEO agency, keep the following in mind:

- **Agency reviews and testimonials:** Explore SEO agency online reviews, case studies and client testimonials. These resources offer insights into the agency’s track record and client satisfaction. Look for patterns in feedback, such as detailed testimonials and consistently positive reviews indicating a good SEO company.
- **Examine case studies** : Case studies are especially valuable because they showcase real-world examples of the agency’s work. They give a clear idea of how a reputable agency tackles specific challenges and the results it’s achieved for similar businesses. For example, a detailed case study on a successful local SEO campaign can demonstrate capabilities in driving regional market growth.
- **Transparency** : Transparency is a cornerstone of a successful SEO partnership. When working with our clients, transparency in our strategies has been key to building long-term partnerships. Choose an agency that’s open about the processes, tools and techniques it uses. Avoid agencies that are vague about their methods or promise guaranteed results without explaining their approach.

To evaluate the expertise and experience of an SEO firm, also consider the following:

- Key indicators of a reputable SEO agency include industry recognition, relevant certifications, and a proven track record in delivering results.
- Think about the agency’s experience in your specific industry. An agency that understands the nuances of your sector will be better equipped to develop a tailored solution to your needs.

Our extensive industry experience has equipped us with the knowledge to address complex SEO challenges.

## Understanding the Agency’s SEO Process

A successful SEO campaign hinges on a well-rounded strategy with several key components working together to achieve your business goals. The agency you work with should be willing to share how they implement each of these:

- **In-depth SEO audits** : The first step of an effective SEO strategy involves thoroughly analysing your site’s technical health and identifying issues that could negatively impact your search engine rankings. From site speed to mobile optimisation, a detailed audit lays the groundwork for subsequent SEO efforts.
- **Keyword research** : Keyword research is a cornerstone of any SEO strategy. Targeted keywords must align both with your audience’s search intent and business objectives. Focusing on high-intent keywords makes you capture traffic more likely to convert, driving meaningful results for your business.
- **On-page and off-page optimisation** : A balanced approach to on-page and off-page optimisation is crucial. On-page efforts include optimising content, meta tags and internal linking structures. Off-page strategies focus on building high-quality backlinks and enhancing your site’s authority. Combined on-page and off-page strategies work together to ensure your website is search engine-friendly and valuable to users.
- **Continuous performance monitoring** : SEO isn’t a one-time effort. Constant monitoring and adjustments are needed to adapt to changing search engine algorithms and larger market trends. Regular performance tracking lets you fine-tune strategies to maintain and improve rankings over time.
- **Tailored methodology** : Our SEO process involves a tailored approach aligning with your business goals. By combining rigorous audits, precise keyword research and a strategic mix of on-page and off-page techniques, we ensure we’re optimising every aspect of your SEO strategy for success.

## Communication and Customer Service

Communication is necessary for a campaign’s success. You want clear, consistent communication from your agency so you’re always informed about the strategies being implemented, progress being made, and adjustments required to achieve your objectives.

An SEO agency prioritising transparent communication will provide regular updates through structured reports, scheduled meetings and accessible communication channels. With transparency, you can make informed decisions and ensure SEO efforts align with your business’s evolving needs.

We’ve developed a communication framework that includes weekly progress reports, monthly strategy reviews, and direct access to a dedicated account manager. Our clients stay informed, and this approach fosters a collaborative environment, encouraging feedback integrated into the strategy.

### Customer Service Goes Beyond Support

Customer service in an SEO agency goes beyond resolving issues—it’s about proactively managing your account to anticipate challenges and opportunities.

Top-tier SEO agencies offer more than reactive support. They provide strategic guidance, anticipate market shifts and suggest innovative approaches to stay ahead of the competition.

Our customer service model includes proactive account management, where we regularly review your business goals and adjust our strategies accordingly.

Choosing an SEO agency with strong communication and customer service capabilities ensures your campaign is managed with the adaptability and attention required for sustained success in a competitive digital landscape.

## Pricing and SEO Budget When Choosing an Agency

You want to understand the available pricing models when evaluating SEO agency costs. SEO pricing will often fall into three main categories:

- **Monthly retainers** : This is a common pricing model in which a client pays a fixed monthly fee for ongoing SEO services. It is ideal for businesses that want long-term SEO strategies that require continuous optimisation and management.
- **Project-based pricing** : Some agencies offer pricing based on specific projects, such as a website audit, content creation or link-building campaign. This model suits companies with specific, defined, one-off SEO needs.
- **Performance-based pricing** : Although less common in this SEO pricing model, clients pay based on achieved results, like keyword rankings or organic increase. This comes with risks, like overemphasising short-term gains at the expense of long-term strategy.

### The Importance of ROI

For enterprise-level clients, the focus shouldn’t be solely on the initial cost but on the return on investment (ROI). High-quality SEO services require a significant investment, but the long-term gains far outweigh the upfront cost. An effective SEO strategy should deliver sustained organic traffic growth, improved brand visibility, and increased revenue.

Be cautious of agencies offering low-cost SEO services. These services often have hidden risks, such as blackhead techniques, poor-quality content or ineffective link-building practices.

Although the initial cost might be lower, the long-term damage to your site’s reputation and rankings can be costly.

We’ve countered clients who initially opted for low-cost SEO services only to face setbacks, including search engine penalties. Rebuilding trust with search engines and recovering lost rankings required a more substantial investment than they would have initially spent on a reputable SEO agency.

## Red Flags When Choosing an SEO Agency

When evaluating agencies, it’s important to be aware of red flags indicating a disreputable provider. The warning signs could reveal a reliance on unethical practices or a lack of genuine expertise.

One of the most prominent red flags is guaranteeing #1 rankings in an unrealistic time frame. SEO is a long-term strategy. Any agency promising quick results is likely cutting corners or using tactics that could harm your site’s credibility.

Red flags to watch for, along with guaranteed rankings in a short window of time, include:

- [Black Hat SEO techniques](https://www.semrush.com/blog/black-hat-seo/?kw=&cmp=US_SRCH_DSA_Blog_EN&label=dsa_pagefeed&Network=g&Device=c&utm_content=683861103833&kwid=aud-973005362103:dsa-2263819780519&cmpid=18348486859&agpid=156312208213&BU=Core&extid=97592280592&adpos=&gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAjwlbu2BhA3EiwA3yXyu0D_kf_y7W5IM0vDiW3i_FyTRUTbTqDP034lHG9hCMkkSJnLwRMFJRoCkwoQAvD_BwE) , such as keyword stuffing, cloaking, and private blog networks (PBNs), can lead to penalties.
- An unwillingness to explain SEO strategies or share detailed reports.
- Contracts with unclear terms, hidden fees or long-term commitments without a defined exit strategy.
- Agencies that don’t provide regular, detailed reporting.
- Promises of quick fixes rather than a focus on sustainable growth.

## Making the Final Decision When Choosing the Best SEO Agency

As you narrow down your options, focus on the key factors that matter most: the agency’s expertise, experience in your industry, transparency in communication and alignment with your business goals. A reputable SEO agency will demonstrate an ability to deliver results and prioritise ethical practices and long-term growth over quick fixes.

Choosing an SEO agency is about more than just achieving initial results. It’s about sustaining and improving those results over time. SEO is a continuous process. It requires ongoing attention, adaptation to changing algorithms and consistent effort to stay ahead of the competition.

Before finalising your decision, set clear expectations and agree on KPIs with the agency. KPIs should be specific, measurable and aligned with your business objectives.

Common KPIs include organic traffic growth, keyword rankings, conversion rates and ROI. Establishing these benchmarks upfront keeps you and the agency on the same page, and that progress can be objectively measured over time.

In addition, discuss the reporting structure and frequency with the agency to ensure you receive regular performance updates and insights into how strategies evolve.
